questions.question:
You are developing a Power Apps app.  
  
The app must retrieve data from an API that requires two-factor authentication.  
  
You need to configure authentication. Which authentication type should you implement?
questions.explanation:
OAuth supports interactive user authentication through an identity provider, including two-factor authentication, and issues access tokens for the API. Microsoft documentation identifies OAuth as required to support Microsoft Entra ID conditional-access configurations such as two-factor authentication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authenticate with Microsoft Dataverse web services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authentication)

You develop code that will update existing records in a table.  
  
The update must be performed by using the alternate key configured for the table.  
  
You need to carry out the update.  
  
Which two requests should you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Dataverse alternate keys can identify a table record through an Entity object's `KeyAttributes` rather than its primary GUID. `UpdateRequest` updates the existing record identified this way. `UpsertRequest` also locates a record by its alternate key and updates it when it exists; it creates a record only when no matching record exists.

**Learn more:** [Use an alternate key to reference a record](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-alternate-key-reference-record) · [Use Upsert to Create or Update a Record in Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-upsert-insert-update-record)

questions.question:
You need to configure the mobile app so that it meets the requirements for phone entries.  
  
Which expression should you use?
questions.explanation:
`IsNumeric` tests whether a value is numeric and returns a Boolean, enabling validation of a phone entry as numeric input.\
\
**Learn more:** [IsNumeric function - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-isnumeric)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a model-driven app. You run Solution checker, and the tool displays this error:  
  
> Solution checker fails to export solutions with model-driven app components.  
  
You need to resolve the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Manually export the solution before running Solution checker
Assign the Environment Maker security role to the Power Apps Checker application user
Assign the System Administrator security role to your user ID
Disable the Power Apps Checker application user
Assign the Environment Maker security role to your user ID

questions.explanation:
Solution Checker exports an unmanaged solution for analysis. Model-driven app components can fail that export when the Power Apps Checker application user lacks the role-based access needed for the app. Assigning the Environment Maker security role to that application user supplies the required access.

**Learn more:** [Improve component performance, stability, and reliability with solution checker](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/use-powerapps-checker)

questions.question:
You are building a model-driven app. You create JavaScript code that displays a message when a record is saved.  
  
You need to configure the related JavaScript web resource name while adding the event handler to the form.  
  
Which field should you use?
questions.explanation:
A form event handler uses the Library field to specify the JavaScript web resource. The Function field identifies the particular function in that library, while Event Type specifies when it runs, such as On Save.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure model-driven app form event handlers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/configure-event-handlers-legacy) · [Events in forms and grids in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/events-forms-grids)

questions.question:
You are building a model-driven app. You create JavaScript code that displays a message when a record is saved.  
  
You need to configure the related JavaScript web resource name while adding the event handler to the form.  
  
Which field should you use?

options.text: In the development instance, make changes to the solutions that are deployed in the production instance, export the solutions as managed solutions, and import the managed solutions into the production instance.
In the development instance, highlight the solution you want to make changes to, select Clone a Patch, make changes, export the solution, and import the solution into the production instance.
Export all managed solutions from the development instance and import the solutions into the production instance.
In the production instance, import solutions with the same version number or higher when updating solutions.

questions.explanation:
Managed solutions are intended for production, whereas unmanaged solutions are typically used during development. A development solution can therefore be modified, exported as a managed solution, and imported into production. An unmanaged solution can also be cloned into a patch; the modified patch can be exported as managed and imported over its managed parent solution in production.

**Learn more:** [Import solutions in Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/import-update-export-solutions) · [Create patches to simplify solution updates with Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/create-patches-simplify-solution-updates)

questions.question:
You need to manage errors in `UpdateRecord.js`.  
  
Which code segment should be added at line UR04?
questions.explanation: JavaScript handles exceptions with a `catch (error)` block. The caught error object exposes its message through `error.message`, so `catch(error) { alert(\"Caught error: \" + error.message);}` provides valid error handling.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is creating multiple plug-ins.  
  
One plug-in continues to fail. You need to debug the plug-in.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Highlight the plug-in step and select Debug in the Plug-in Registration tool
Copy the .pdb file into the server/bin/assembly folder
Select Start Profiling in the Plug-in Registration tool
Attach the debugger to the w3wp.exe process

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Dataverse debugging uses Plug-in Profiler: install the profiler, start profiling on the registered plug-in step to capture an execution profile, and select **Debug** in the Plug-in Registration Tool to replay that profile locally for debugging.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Debug a plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/tutorial-debug-plug-in)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop a model-driven app. You add the following users as members of the Sales Microsoft Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) security group: User1, User2, and User3.  
  
The Sales Azure AD security group is linked to an existing Microsoft Dataverse Azure AD security group team associated with the Sales security role. You assign the appropriate licenses to each user.  
  
User1 does not appear in the app's Team Members subgrid. User2 and User3 appear in the subgrid.  
  
You need to make sure that User1 can use the model-driven app.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Change the membership of the Sales Azure AD Security group to Dynamic User.
Change the membership type for User1 to Owner in the Azure AD security group.
Create an Owner team for the members of the Sales Azure AD group.
Ask User1 to sign into the model-driven app.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra group-team members are dynamically added to the Dataverse group team when they access the environment. A licensed member inherits the security role assigned to that group team at runtime, so signing in to the model-driven app provisions User1's team membership and access.

**Learn more:** [Manage group teams - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/manage-group-teams) · [Work with Microsoft Entra ID group teams (Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/aad-group-team)

questions.question:
You create a custom API as part of a solution that will be available on Microsoft AppSource.  
  
You need to prevent others from using Dataverse code-generation tools to create classes that use the messages for your custom API.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set Allowed Custom Processing Step Type to None.

questions.explanation:
Setting **Is Private** to **Yes** hides the custom API from the Web API `$metadata` document and prevents Dataverse code-generation tools from creating classes for its messages.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and use custom APIs (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/custom-api)

questions.question:
Solution: Use access team templates and grant access to members in the two departments.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Access team templates enable record-level sharing with specified users. Adding employees from both departments to an opportunity’s access team grants them the template’s access rights, allowing cross-department collaboration on that specific opportunity without broadly exposing all department records.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a team template to control access rights for automatically created teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/create-team-template-add-entity-form) · [Access Teams and Owner Teams for Record Sharing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-access-teams-owner-teams-collaborate-share-information)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a security role with organization-level access to opportunities. Assign this security role to all members of the two departments that require access.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Organization-level access grants access to all Opportunity records across the organization regardless of business-unit membership. Assigning that role to every member of both departments exposes all department opportunities, rather than only the opportunities that need to be shared for collaboration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Security roles in Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/admin/security-roles-privileges?view=op-9-1)

questions.question:
Solution: Use position-hierarchy security and define the two departments as positions.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Position hierarchy security grants access down a direct ancestor path: users in higher positions can access records owned by users in lower positions. It does not provide mutual, opportunity-specific collaboration between two departments merely by representing them as positions. Sharing the opportunity or using an appropriate team-based access model is required for employees in both departments to work on the same record.\
\
**Learn more:** [Hierarchy security - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/hierarchy-security)

questions.question:
Solution: Share the individual opportunity being worked on by members of one department with every member of the second department, granting them the appropriate permissions.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Record-level sharing can grant the required access rights to users in another department for a specific opportunity. This enables those employees to view and work on that opportunity without broadly exposing all departmental opportunity records.\
\
**Learn more:** [Share rows with a user or team](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/user/share-row) · [Use access teams and owner teams to collaborate and share information](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-access-teams-owner-teams-collaborate-share-information)

questions.question:
A company is building a Power Apps portal to collaborate with vendors.  
  
You need to add custom portal functionality by using JavaScript code.  
  
Which two portal entities can be used? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Power Pages portal functionality can be extended with client-side JavaScript on web pages, and an entity list’s configuration includes a custom JavaScript area for scripts that act on the rendered list. Web roles are security assignments rather than code-hosting entities, and web resources are not the portal configuration entity for this purpose.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage web pages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/configure/web-page) · [Add custom JavaScript to a list](https://learn.microsoft.com/ga-ie/power-pages/configure/add-custom-javascript-list)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is designing a solution for an international organization.  
  
The solution must support multiple UI languages and currencies.  
  
You need to move components so that they are included in the solution.  
  
Which three component types can you move? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A scheduled Power Automate cloud flow can be solution-aware and included in a solution. A custom entity (custom Dataverse table) is a solution component. Changes to a security role can also be exported in a solution for use in another implementation. UI language availability and currencies enabled for an environment are environment-level settings, not transportable solution components.

**Learn more:** [Create or edit a security role to manage access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/create-edit-security-role) · [Organize your solutions in Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/organize-solutions)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a JavaScript function that runs when the account record form is saved. Use the JavaScript function's Web API to create the contact record.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Client-side JavaScript registered for a model-driven app form runs in response to form events, including form save events. An account created through the external Azure Function integration bypasses the UI form and therefore does not invoke that JavaScript, so no default contact is guaranteed for every account record. [Microsoft Learn: Apply business logic using client scripting in model-driven apps using JavaScript](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/client-scripting)\
\
**Learn more:** [Apply business logic using client scripting in model-driven apps using JavaScript](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/client-scripting)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a plug-in that runs when an account record is created. Use the Organization service to create the contact record.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Dataverse plug-ins can be registered to respond to the `Create` message for a table, and plug-in code can use `IOrganizationService` to create another table row. Therefore, an account-create plug-in can automatically create the required related contact regardless of whether the account originated in the UI or through the integrated external process.\
\
**Learn more:** [Event Framework in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/event-framework) · [IOrganizationService.Create(Entity) Method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.iorganizationservice.create?view=dataverse-sdk-latest)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a cloud flow that runs when an account record is created. Use the Dataverse connector to create the contact record.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Dataverse **When a row is added, modified or deleted** trigger runs when a row in the selected table is created, including rows created through an external integration. Without a condition that limits the flow to accounts created by users in the UI, the flow also creates contacts for accounts created by the Azure Function.\
\
**Learn more:** [Trigger flows when a row is added, modified, or deleted](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/dataverse/create-update-delete-trigger) · [Microsoft Dataverse connector reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/commondataserviceforapps/)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a custom API that is bound to the account table and uses a plug-in. Use the Organization service to create the contact record.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An entity-bound custom API runs only when that API is explicitly invoked for an account record; binding supplies a `Target` account reference to the API plug-in. It does not automatically execute when an account record is created through the UI or an external Azure Function. Therefore, the solution cannot ensure creation of a default contact for every account creation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and use custom APIs (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/custom-api) · [IOrganizationService.Create(Entity) Method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.iorganizationservice.create?view=dataverse-sdk-latest)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a custom API that is bound to the account table and uses a plug-in. Use the Organization service to create the contact record.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?

options.text: Create a new developer environment. Register the plug-in.
Back up and restore the environment.
Create a new sandbox environment Register the plug-in.

questions.explanation:
A developer environment provides an isolated Dataverse environment for development and testing without copying the German environment’s data to North America. Developer environments created through sign-up use the Microsoft Entra tenant home location. By contrast, Dataverse environment copy and restore operations require the source and target environments to be in the same region, so they cannot transfer the German environment to the tenant’s North American default region.

**Learn more:** [Power Platform environments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/environments-overview) · [Copy an environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/copy-environment)

A company needs a plug-in that sends multiple requests to an external web service. The plug-in must not time out if the web service encounters problems or responds slowly.  
  
You need to create the plug-in.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign the IOrganizationService object to a member variable.
Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
Register the plug-in step once for each web service request.
Set the HTTP connection KeepAlive property to false.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse plug-ins are short-lived sandbox executions, so persistent HTTP connections generally provide no benefit. If a persistent connection has expired, attempts to reuse it can trigger retries and prolonged execution. Setting the HTTP connection `KeepAlive` property to `false` avoids that failure mode for outbound web-service calls.

**Learn more:** [Set KeepAlive to false when interacting with external hosts in a plug-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/set-keepalive-false-interacting-external-hosts-plugin) · [Access external web services (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/access-web-services)

questions.question:
You must connect to the background check API.  
  
Which mechanism should you use?
questions.explanation:
A Power Automate flow can call an external background-check API through a custom connector. Custom connectors wrap REST or SOAP APIs and expose their operations as flow actions, including authentication and request/response definitions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Custom connectors overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/connectors/custom-connectors/) · [Build and certify custom connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/developer/register-custom-api)

questions.question:
A company has a form in a model-driven app. Many users work with the form.  
  
Users report that the form takes too long to load completely.  
  
You need to assess the form design to improve load performance.  
  
Which three control types can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Model-driven app forms support Timeline, Quick View Form, and IFRAME as controls that can be added to a form. A lookup is a column type, not an insertable form control type in this context.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of the model-driven app form editor user interface for Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/form-editor-user-interface-legacy)

questions.question:
You create a plug-in to validate data.  
  
Users report that the validation is not working as expected.  
  
You need to debug the plug-in.  
  
Which tool should you use?

options.text: Power Platform Tools for Visual Studio

questions.explanation:
Plug-in Profiler captures a Dataverse plug-in’s execution context and enables that execution to be replayed in Visual Studio for debugging.\
\
**Learn more:** [Debug plug-ins (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/debug-plug-in)

questions.question:
You need to select a technology to access the Web API.  
  
Which technology should you choose?

options.text: Canvas app that uses the custom connector
Plug-in that contacts the Web API
Power Automate flow that uses the custom connector
Webhook that contacts the Web API

questions.explanation:
A Power Automate flow can use the custom connector to call the Web API and automatically update the eligible Dataverse Account records. Custom connectors are designed to expose tailored web-service actions for use in Power Automate flows.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use a custom connector from a flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/use-custom-connector-flow)

questions.question:
You need to identify which component to add to the solution to fix the account-records import error.  
  
Which component should you add?
questions.explanation:
A custom connector is the solution component that defines the Web API actions used by the Power Automate flow. It must be included in, and imported with, the solution so the target environment has the connector required by the flow; connections are created or configured separately in each environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create custom connectors in solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/customconnectorssolutions)

questions.question:
You need to set up the row filter for the Dataverse trigger.  
  
Which filter should be used?
questions.explanation:
The Dataverse trigger's **Filter rows** setting uses an OData expression. `new_dataid ne null` evaluates true only for Account rows with a value in the `new_dataid` column, satisfying the requirement to update only records that contain a DataId. [Microsoft Dataverse connector reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/commondataserviceforapps/), [Filter rows by using OData](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query/filter-rows)\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Dataverse connector reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/commondataserviceforapps/) · [Filter rows by using OData](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query/filter-rows)

questions.question:
You need to ensure that data returned by the Web API matches the appropriate environment.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: records in a new configuration table

questions.explanation:
Power Platform environment variables store configuration values that can differ between development, test, and production while the solution components remain unchanged. Setting the environment-specific value during deployment lets the Web API use the endpoint for the correct environment without hardcoding it.\
\
**Learn more:** [Environment variables for Power Platform overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/environmentvariables)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to add visual hints to the custom connector.  
  
What should you do? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: In the custom connector, update the name of the policy template.
Extend the Open API definition of the Web API for the EnvironmentName parameter.
Extend the Open API definition of the Web API for the DataId parameter.
In the custom connector, update the description for the DataId parameter.

questions.explanation:
A custom connector displays a parameter’s `description` as helpful text within its input box. The DataId parameter can receive that description either by extending its OpenAPI definition or by updating the parameter description in the custom connector. EnvironmentName metadata and a policy-template name do not provide a visual hint for the user-entered DataId value.

**Learn more:** [Learn best practices for string fields](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/connector-string-guidance) · [Create a custom connector with an OpenAPI extension](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/openapi-extensions)

questions.question:
You need to determine the cause of a 404 error when connecting to the production instance of the Web API.  
  
What do you identify?

options.text: The web service lacks data for the record.
The host name in the URL is missing a valid value.

questions.explanation:
The API returns HTTP 404 when the supplied DataId is not found, so the web service does not contain enrichment data for that record. A 404 status indicates that the requested resource cannot be found.\
\
**Learn more:** [RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics — 404 Not Found](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-404-not-found)

questions.question:
You need to create an application for deployment to other pharmacies.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Recreate customizations in a new environment.
Create a customer connector to connect the pharmacies' systems to the company's systems.
Export the solution as a managed solution.
Write a Web API to move customizations.

questions.explanation:
A managed solution packages the application and its customizations so they can be exported and imported into other Dataverse environments. Managed solutions are the appropriate deployment artifact for environments that are not the solution’s development environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Introduction to solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/introduction-solutions) · [Application lifecycle management (ALM) basics with Microsoft Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/basics-alm)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a plug-in in Dataverse to carry out complex data calculations in near real time.  
  
The calculations frequently run for more than five minutes, causing the plug-in to time out.  
  
You need to recommend a suitable replacement component.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Azure Functions provides event-driven serverless compute for custom calculation logic outside the Dataverse plug-in execution pipeline. Dataverse message operations have a hard execution-time limit and long-running operations should not be performed in plug-ins; moving the calculations to a function avoids that plug-in constraint while preserving near-real-time processing.

**Learn more:** [Analyze plug-in performance (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/analyze-performance) · [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration)

questions.question:

What should you do?

options.text: Navigate to Customize the System and export everything to a managed solution.

questions.explanation:

\
**Learn more:** [Application lifecycle management basics with Microsoft Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/basics-alm) · [Managed properties](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/managed-properties-alm)

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's communications department plans to add a publicly accessible survey page to the company’s public website.  
  
You must add the new survey page to the company’s public website and capture its data in a Microsoft Dataverse environment.  
  
Explicit user credentials must not be required to write survey data to Dataverse.  
  
You need to implement authentication. Which authentication mechanism should you implement?
questions.explanation:
A client secret enables confidential-client, server-to-server authentication for a Microsoft Entra application or service principal. The application can be represented by an application user in Dataverse and assigned only the permissions needed to create the survey data, without requiring credentials from public website users.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Register an app with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/walkthrough-register-app-azure-active-directory) · [Authenticate with Microsoft Dataverse web services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company intends to build an order-processing app. When orders are created, the app will execute complex business logic and integrate with several external systems.  
  
Orders with a large number of line items can require up to six minutes to complete. Processing for each order must finish in a single operation to prevent records from being left in an incomplete state.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for the company.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: an asynchronous workflow that uses a custom workflow activity
a real-time workflow that uses a custom action
a webhook that connects to an Azure Function

questions.explanation:
A real-time workflow using a custom action executes in the main Dataverse operation pipeline, allowing the work to participate in the same transaction. If processing fails, the transaction can roll back, preventing incomplete order records. Asynchronous workflows and plug-ins execute after the initiating operation, while webhook processing is external to the transaction.

**Learn more:** [Use Custom Process Actions with code (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/workflow-custom-actions) · [Use Plug-ins to Extend Business Processes (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/plug-ins)

questions.question:
You need to fix the address-validation API error.  
  
Which connection method should you use?

options.text: an Azure function triggered by a webhook
a custom connector used in a cloud flow
a plug-in attached to a custom action called from JavaScript

questions.explanation:
A custom connector exposes an API’s operations as actions that a Power Automate cloud flow can invoke, including APIs for which no prebuilt connector exists. This provides the appropriate authenticated, reusable connection to an address-validation API.\
\
**Learn more:** [Build and certify custom connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/developer/register-custom-api)

options.text: Select the Portal Management app and then select Edit.

questions.explanation:
A portal page’s layout can be changed in the portal design studio, which is opened by editing the portal app. Advanced page configuration, including page templates and web-page metadata, can also be performed in the Portal Management app; because it is a model-driven app, it is launched by selecting **Play**. The **Manage** action is for administering the portal rather than authoring a page layout.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A travel company has a Common Data Service (CDS) environment.  
  
The company needs the following:  
  
- Custom entities to record the regions that clients have traveled to.  
- The dates on which clients traveled to those regions.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783811278610-zrcrkr1x.png)  
  
You need to create the entities and relationships that meet the requirements.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a N:N relationship from Contact to the Region entity.
Create a 1:N relationship from the ContactRegion intersect entity and Region.
Create an intersect entity named ContactRegion and create 1:N relationships to Contact and Region.
On the main form for ContactRegion, add lookup fields for Contact and Region, and a date field for the visit date.
Create a 1:N relationship from Contact to the Region entity.

questions.explanation:
A custom intersect entity is needed when the relationship between Contact and Region must store additional data, such as the visit date. Contact and Region each have a one-to-many relationship to ContactRegion, making ContactRegion the many-side record that stores lookups to both entities and the date field. The Region entity must exist before it can participate in that design. A built-in N:N relationship cannot store custom columns on its relationship table.

**Learn more:** [Use complex relationships with Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/architecture/reference-architectures/complex-relationships-dataverse) · [Create many-to-many table relationships overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-edit-nn-relationships)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Microsoft Dataverse rollup fields to calculate insurance exposure and risk profiles for its customers.  
  
Users report that rollup-field values are not updated when new insurance policies are created.  
  
You need to recalculate the rollup-field values immediately after a policy is created.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create new fields on the customer entity for insurance exposure and risk. Write a workflow process that is triggered when a new policy record is created to calculate the sum of values from policy records.
Create new calculated fields on the customer entity for insurance exposure and risk. Configure the formula to calculate the sum of values from policy records.
Change the frequency of the Calculate Rollup Field recurring job from every hour to every five minutes.
Create new fields on the customer entity for insurance exposure and risk. Write a plug-in that is triggered whenever a new policy is created.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse rollup columns are updated asynchronously by a recurring system job, with a minimum recurrence of one hour, so they cannot be refreshed immediately by increasing the job frequency. A plug-in triggered by creation of a policy can calculate the required aggregates and write the customer fields immediately. [Define rollup columns with Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/define-rollup-fields)

**Learn more:** [Define rollup columns with Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/define-rollup-fields)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are testing security in a model-driven app. The environment’s business-unit structure consists of a top-level business unit with three business units—BusA, BusB, and BusC—directly beneath it.  
  
BusA users must be able to view records only in their own business unit.  
  
You find that BusA users have security roles from BusB and BusC assigned. These BusA users can view records in those business units. All security-role privileges are configured at the Business Unit level.  
  
You need to fix the record-access issue.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Turn off the feature that controls record ownership across business units.
Create a security role for BusA users in the parent business unit with privileges set to Business Unit level.
Move BusA users to the parent business unit. Assign security roles with Parent Child Business Units privileges.
Ensure security role privileges are set to User level.

questions.explanation:
When Record ownership across business units is enabled, Dataverse allows a user to receive security roles from other business units; a Business Unit-level privilege in those roles grants access to records in the corresponding business units. Disable that feature and provide BusA users an appropriate Business Unit-level role through the parent business-unit hierarchy, so their role-based access is limited to BusA. Parent:Child Business Units scope would grant access to multiple child business units, while User scope would restrict access to user-owned records rather than business-unit records.

**Learn more:** [Assign security roles - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/assign-security-roles) · [Security concepts in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/wp-security-cds)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing C# code to create an alternate key on a table using two columns: Order ID and Order Date. The table contains thousands of records.  
  
You use the `CreateEntityKey` message to create the key. When you retrieve `EntityKeyMetadata.EntityKeyIndexStatus`, it returns `Failed`.  
  
You need to resolve the index-creation issue.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Delete duplicate combination values in Order ID and Order Date.

questions.explanation:
An alternate key requires a unique index across its key columns. Existing rows with the same Order ID and Order Date combination prevent that unique index from being created. Remove those duplicate composite values before reactivating the failed key-creation request. Microsoft documents reactivation as the step to take after the cause of a failed alternate-key index build has been corrected.

**Learn more:** [Work with alternate keys (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/define-alternate-keys-entity)

You are developing a model-driven app for a company that sells sporting goods. You add a button to a page that shows product information.  
  
The button must copy the information for the selected product and create a record in the data source. You add the following code to the button. (Line numbers are included only for reference.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783826706828-qp0xbe47.png)  
  
You need to complete the code.  
  
Which function should you insert on line 01?
questions.explanation:
`Patch` creates or modifies records in a data source. `Patch(Products, Defaults(Products), { ... })` uses the default record for `Products` as the base record, so it creates a new record populated with the selected product’s Name, Description, Type, and Price.

**Learn more:** [Patch function - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-patch)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s communications department plans to add a publicly accessible survey page to the company’s public website.  
  
You must add the survey page to the company’s public website and capture data from the page in a Microsoft Dataverse environment.  
  
Explicit user credentials must not be required to write survey data to Dataverse.  
  
You need to implement authentication.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should you implement?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Dataverse Web API access uses OAuth 2.0. A public website can use server-to-server application authentication, in which the application obtains an OAuth access token and writes data as its application user, without requiring survey respondents to provide credentials. A certificate can serve as an application's credential in such a flow, but OAuth 2.0 is the authentication mechanism used to access Dataverse.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate to Microsoft Dataverse with the Web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/authenticate-web-api) · [Build web applications using server-to-server authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/build-web-applications-server-server-s2s-authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to populate records in a Microsoft Dataverse entity that includes an option set field.  
  
The source system contains the option-set label but not its matching integer value. You are using a non-.NET programming language and need to determine the integer value for the option set.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Web API and use a PicklistAttibuteMetadata request.
Use the Organization service and execute a RetrieveOptionSetRequest request.
Use Web API and use an InsertOptionValue action.
Use the Organization service and execute a RetrieveAttributeRequest request.

questions.explanation:
The Dataverse Web API can query a `PicklistAttributeMetadata` definition and retrieve its `OptionSet` options. Each option’s metadata contains both its localized label and integer `Value`, allowing the source label to be mapped to the value required when creating the record. `RetrieveOptionSetRequest` applies only to global choices, and `InsertOptionValue` creates rather than retrieves an option. Microsoft’s Web API metadata sample shows retrieving a choice column’s options through `PicklistAttributeMetadata` and its `OptionSet`.

**Learn more:** [Web API table schema operations sample (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/web-api-metadata-operations-sample) · [Query table definitions using the Web API (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query-metadata-web-api)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a custom page that serves as a contextual dialog in a model-driven app.  
  
The app must receive two contextual parameters by passing a concatenated string. The string must use the pipe (`|`) symbol with the `recordId` parameter.  
  
You need to compose formulas that extract the parameter information.  
  
Which two formulas should you compose? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
`Find` returns the one-based position of the pipe delimiter. `Left` with that position minus one returns the characters before the delimiter, and `Right` with the total string length minus the delimiter position returns the characters after it. Power Fx `Left` and `Right` extract the beginning and ending portions of a string, respectively.

**Learn more:** [Left, Mid, and Right functions - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-left-mid-right) · [Find function - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-find)

You need to configure the system to enable automation for referrals.  
  
Which two approaches can accomplish this goal? Each correct selection provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Azure Function that uses the Discovery service
Azure Function that uses a listener

questions.explanation:
A Power Automate flow can automatically run when a Dataverse row is created, updated, or deleted. Dataverse can also publish event context to Azure Service Bus, where a listener such as an Azure Function can process the event and perform the required automation. The Discovery service locates environments and does not provide event processing.

**Learn more:** [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration) · [Trigger flows when a row is added, modified, or deleted](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/dataverse/create-update-delete-trigger)

questions.question:
Solution: Register a webhook that uses the REST API as its endpoint. Wait for the webhook to retry automatically if a failure occurs.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Dataverse WebHook delivery makes one additional attempt only when the endpoint returns HTTP 502, 503, or 504. An HTTP 500 response does not trigger that automatic retry behavior, so this approach does not meet a requirement to retry when the REST API returns status code 500.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use webhooks to create external handlers for server events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-webhooks)
