You have a Power Automate flow that uses an HTTP action to connect to a web service and update a Microsoft Dataverse record with the result.  
  
You must modify the flow so that an email is sent if the web-service connection fails.  
  
You need to update the flow.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution. Choose two.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure the send email step to run when the previous step fails.
Add a send email step after the update Dataverse record step.
Add a send email step after the HTTP step.
Update the HTTP step settings and set the retry policy to: None.

questions.explanation:
Place the email action directly after the HTTP action and configure its Run after setting to run only when that preceding HTTP action has failed. Run after conditions support an alternate error-handling path, including sending a notification after an action fails. The Dataverse update is not reached after a failed HTTP action, and a retry policy does not replace the required failure-notification path.

**Learn more:** [Employ robust error handling - Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/guidance/coding-guidelines/error-handling) · [Fix connection failures in cloud flows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/fix-connection-failures)

questions.question:
You create a cloud flow that processes a list of records by using a loop.  
  
You need to decide when to initialize a variable used to process those records.  
  
When should you initialize the variable?

options.text: after the first use of the variable inside the loop
before the first use of the variable inside the loop

questions.explanation:
Power Automate variables must be initialized at the global flow level, rather than inside loops, and must exist before loop actions can use them. Initialize the variable before the loop so every iteration can reference or update the same variable.\
\
**Learn more:** [Store and manage values in variables in Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/create-variable-store-values)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are mapping data from an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system to Microsoft Dataverse.  
  
During mapping, you must reference the Name and Email from the ERP system to ensure records are unique.  
  
You need to create an alternate key that references the Name and Email columns.  
  
How should you create the key?

options.text: Add a Power Apps command function.
Add column to the Account table in Dataverse.
Create a key in the Account table in Dataverse.

questions.explanation:
A Dataverse alternate key is created on the relevant table and can use a combination of columns to uniquely identify records during external-system integration. Creating a key on the Account table with the Name and Email columns enforces that composite uniqueness.

**Learn more:** [Define alternate keys to reference rows with Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/define-alternate-keys-reference-records) · [Work with alternate keys (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/define-alternate-keys-entity)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A multinational company mandates that every phone number use the format: country code + area code + phone number.  
  
The application design team decides to use a custom Power Apps component framework (PCF) control to ask users for an area code and correctly format the phone number.  
  
You must retrieve the list of valid area codes when a contact record opens and before a user enters a new phone number.  
  
In which function should you call `webAPI.retrieveMultipleRecords`?
questions.explanation:
`updateView` runs when the PCF control’s property bag changes, including when the bound record context is provided or updated. It is therefore the applicable lifecycle function for loading data needed to render the control for the opened contact record. `notifyOutputChanged` merely notifies the framework of changed output, while `getOutputs` returns those output values. The PCF Web API method `retrieveMultipleRecords` retrieves a collection of table records.

**Learn more:** [StandardControl (Power Apps component framework API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/reference/control) · [retrieveMultipleRecords (Power Apps component framework API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/reference/webapi/retrievemultiplerecords)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs a plug-in that issues multiple requests to an external web service. The plug-in must not time out if the web service has problems or responds slowly.  
  
You need to create the plug-in.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
Register the plug-in by using isolation mode = none.
Set the HTTP connection timeout value explicitly to limit how long each connection can remain open.
Register the plug-in step once for each web service request.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse plug-ins should set an appropriate timeout for every external HTTP call. This bounds the time spent waiting for a slow or nonresponsive service, preventing the calls from consuming the plug-in operation’s execution-time budget; synchronous message operations have a hard two-minute completion limit.

**Learn more:** [Access external web services (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/access-web-services) · [Analyze plug-in performance (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/analyze-performance)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a new Microsoft Dataverse plug-in that handles an entity's Update message.  
  
The plug-in logic needs access to the record columns before the operation begins and must compare those columns with the post-update values.  
  
You need to change the solution design to access this information.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the code to the plug-in to read the record from the InputParameters collection.
Register a pre-image by using the Plug-in Registration Tool. Add the code to the plug-in to read the image from the PreEntityImages collection.
Register a post-image by using the Plug-in Registration Tool. Add the code to the plug-in to read the image from the PostEntityImages collection.
Add the code to the plug-in to query the data from Dataverse by using the API call based on the record ID.

questions.explanation:
A pre-image registered for the Update step provides a snapshot of the selected record columns before the core update operation. The plug-in reads those original values from `PreEntityImages` and compares them with the updated column values supplied in the Update request. Entity images are designed for this comparison and avoid an additional Dataverse retrieval.

**Learn more:** [Register a plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/register-plug-in) · [Understand execution context in Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/understand-the-data-context)

options.text: Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
Set the HTTP connection KeepAlive property to false.
Register the plug-in by using isolation mode = none.
Assign the IOrganizationService object to a member variable.

questions.explanation:
For Dataverse plug-ins that call external web services, setting the HTTP connection `KeepAlive` property to `false` prevents reuse of stale persistent connections that can cause lengthy network retries and increased execution times. Microsoft recommends disabling `KeepAlive` for these external plug-in calls.

**Learn more:** [Set KeepAlive to false when interacting with external hosts in a plug-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/set-keepalive-false-interacting-external-hosts-plugin) · [Access external web services (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/access-web-services)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a new app on Power Platform.  
  
The checker fails with an error because security roles are missing. You need to add security roles to the Power Apps Checker application user.  
  
Which two security roles should you add? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The Power Apps Checker application user requires the **Export Customizations** role to export the unmanaged solution for analysis and the **Solution Checker** role to perform the checker service operation. Solution Checker analyzes unmanaged solutions that can be exported from an environment.

**Learn more:** [Improve solution performance, stability and reliability with solution checker](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/use-powerapps-checker) · [Use the Power Apps checker web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/checker-api/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a canvas app that connects to Microsoft Dataverse. You add the Accounts table as a data source for the app and implement a gallery to display information from the Accounts table.  
  
The Accounts table is saved and cached locally in a collection named `collAccounts`. The gallery data must always show accounts that have a name value. The gallery uses the following Power Fx formula:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783898289366-wndkkoii.png)  
  
You deploy the app to production.  
  
Users report that the app does not show the expected number of Account rows.  
  
You need to fix the user issue.  
  
How should you modify the Power Fx formula?

options.text: Filter(Sort(Accounts, 'Account Name', SortOrder.Descending), IsBlank('Account Name') = false)

questions.explanation:
A local collection can represent only the portion of Dataverse data retrieved into the app; `ClearCollect` is nondelegable and can therefore yield incomplete results. Applying the filter and sort directly to the Dataverse `Accounts` table lets Power Apps delegate those operations and retrieve gallery rows as needed. Dataverse supports delegation for `Filter`, text `Sort`, and `IsBlank` on text columns.

**Learn more:** [Understand delegation in a canvas app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/delegation-overview) · [Connect to Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/connections/connection-common-data-service)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure the PCF control to show team members for interview scheduling.  
  
Which two inputs should you use? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: time-zone offset for the job candidate
time-zone offset for the hiring manager

questions.explanation:
The PCF control must display the senior team members who report directly to a hiring manager and sort them so that those whose time zone is closest to the applicant's appear first. To retrieve the correct set of team members the control needs the identifier for the hiring manager (so it can find that manager's direct reports), and to sort by proximity to the applicant it needs the time-zone offset for the job candidate as the reference point. The team members' own time-zone offsets come from the SystemUser table, so they are not passed in; the hiring manager's own offset and the job-posting identifier are not needed for this control.

**Learn more:** [PL-400 study guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/resources/study-guides/pl-400)

options.text: Add a referral source field to the Application table.
Create a new Referral table with required lookup columns to the Contact, SystemUser, and Application tables.
Add a second lookup column to SystemUser for manager referrals to the Application table.
Create a new Referral table with required lookup columns to the Contact, SystemUser, and JobPosting tables.

questions.explanation:
A separate Referral table with required lookups to Contact, SystemUser, and JobPosting records each referral independently, associates it with the candidate, referrer, and position, and does not require an Application record. Lookup columns create many-to-one relationships, allowing a contact to have multiple related referral records. [Create a relationship between tables by using a lookup column — Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-entity-lookup)

**Learn more:** [Create a relationship between tables by using a lookup column — Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-entity-lookup)

questions.question:
You need to fix the issue with the new command button.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Pass ExecutionContext to the function in the action definition.
Pass the value SelectedControl to the function in the action definition.
Select the Pass execution context as first parameter option on the event registration form.
Pass the value PrimaryControl to the function in the action definition.

questions.explanation:
A model-driven app command executed from a form must pass `PrimaryControl` to its JavaScript function to provide the form context. `SelectedControl` supplies grid context, and the form-event setting for passing execution context does not configure a command-bar action.\
\
**Learn more:** [Pass data from a page as a parameter to ribbon actions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/pass-data-page-parameter-ribbon-actions)

questions.question:
You need to identify the cause of the issue reported by the interviewers.  
  
What is the root cause of the issue?

options.text: There was an error in the event pipeline and the entire transaction was rolled back.
There is no plug-in registered to run when an interview record is created.
The plug-in used to synchronize the Person of Interest field from Contact to Interview was not triggered.

questions.explanation: A newly created Interview record for an existing person of interest must have its Person of Interest value synchronized from the related Contact. If that synchronization plug-in does not run when the Interview is created, the Interview field is not updated and the notification plug-in registered for updates to that field does not send an email to the interviewer.

questions.question:
You need to store designations and certifications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Lookup column on the Contact table.
Create a new table that has an N:N relationship with the Contact table.
Create a new table that has an N:1 relationship with the Contact table.
Create a new Choices column on the Contact table.

questions.explanation:
Designations and certifications are reusable records: one contact may hold several, and each designation or certification may be associated with many contacts. An N:N relationship between a new table and the Contact table supports both directions of that association. Microsoft Dataverse many-to-many relationships are intended for cases in which multiple rows in each table can be associated with multiple rows in the other table.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create many-to-many table relationships overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-edit-nn-relationships)

questions.question:
You need to stop the field used by the PCF control from updating the record.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a business rule to clear the field value.
Call the setSubmitMode(‘never’) function on the field.
Disable existing event handlers on the field.

questions.explanation:
A read-only field prevents edits through the form control, and setting an attribute’s submit mode to `never` prevents its data from being submitted when the record is saved. The Power Apps Client API defines `never` as a mode in which column data is never sent during a save.\
\
**Learn more:** [setSubmitMode (Client API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/attributes/setsubmitmode)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a .NET application that loads a large volume of data into a Dataverse table containing one default column value. A synchronous plug-in already applies that same default column value to new rows in the table.  
  
To accelerate the process, you must disable the plug-in while the data load runs. The load must run during business hours and must not affect rows that users might be creating.  
  
You need to perform the operations.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Send the BypassCustomPluginExecution as an optional parameter with the create request.
Send the SuppressCallbackRegistrationExpanderJob as an optional parameter with the request.
Disable the plug-in step prior to starting the data load.
Set the BypassPluginExecution property on the CrmServiceClient.

questions.explanation:
`BypassCustomPluginExecution` bypasses custom synchronous logic for an individual create request, and `CrmServiceClient.BypassPluginExecution` enables that bypass behavior for requests made through that client. Both approaches scope the bypass to the data-load application's operations, so the synchronous plug-in remains active for rows created concurrently by users. The calling identity requires the privilege to bypass custom plug-ins.

**Learn more:** [Bypass custom Dataverse logic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/bypass-custom-business-logic) · [CrmServiceClient.BypassPluginExecution Property](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.tooling.connector.crmserviceclient.bypasspluginexecution?view=dataverse-sdk-latest)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are troubleshooting a newly created canvas app.  
  
Users report that the app loads slowly. You use the Monitor tool to view various events occurring in the app. The events performed in the app do not include formula details.  
  
You need to enable formulas to be included with the Monitor tool events.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the Microsoft Azure Application Insights data source to the canvas app
After each event, implement the trace function within the canvas app
Turn on the Debug published app setting in the canvas app
Validate the Application Insights instrumentation key has been populated in the app object's properties within the canvas app

questions.explanation:
For a published canvas app, Monitor can display events without the source formulas. Enabling **Debug published app** in the app settings publishes source expressions with the app so Monitor can show the formulas associated with events.

**Learn more:** [Debugging canvas apps with Live monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/monitor-canvasapps)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial institution with a Dynamics 365 Sales environment requires the account balance field on the account entity to be visible only to specified users.  
  
You need to configure field security for the account balance field.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Set the field to Read-Only and then publish the entity
Set the field permission Allow Read to Yes and add the users to the members section
Create a security role and add the specific users to the role
Enable field security and then publish the entity

questions.explanation:
Field-level security restricts access to a field through a field security profile. The field must have field security enabled and published, the profile must grant its members the Allow Read permission, and the specified users must be added as members of that profile. A normal security role governs entity and record access rather than the secured field's read permission.

**Learn more:** [Column-level security - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/field-level-security) · [Field level security | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/admin/field-level-security?view=op-9-1)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company relies on a third-party shipping provider to deliver products to customers.  
  
You need to design a custom connector that obtains shipping fees from the shipping company API.  
  
Which three elements must you define for the custom connector? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A custom connector must define how it authenticates to the backend API, the API endpoint/address it calls, and the API contract that describes its operations and data structures. An OpenAPI definition supplies that machine-readable contract; the shipping fee is returned by the defined operation rather than being a separate connector-level reference.

**Learn more:** [Create a custom connector from an OpenAPI definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/connectors/custom-connectors/define-openapi-definition) · [Specify connection parameters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/connectors/custom-connectors/connection-parameters)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A Microsoft Dataverse database has two custom tables named TableA and TableB, configured as follows:  
  
- A one-to-many relationship exists between TableA and TableB.  
- A lookup to TableA is displayed on a TableB form.  
- Both tables are components of an unmanaged solution.  
- Both tables are components in a Power BI report.  
  
An error occurs when you try to delete TableA.  
  
You need to delete the table.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Remove TableA from the Power BI report.
Remove the relationship between TableA and TableB.
Remove TableA from the unmanaged solution.
Remove the lookup field to TableA on the TableB form.

questions.explanation:
A custom Dataverse table cannot be deleted while another component depends on it. The one-to-many relationship and its TableB lookup create that dependency. Removing the relationship removes the dependency; merely removing the lookup from a form leaves the lookup column and relationship intact. An unmanaged solution is only a container for unmanaged components, so removing a table from it does not delete the underlying dependency.

**Learn more:** [Delete a table - Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-delete-entity) · [Removing dependencies overview in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/removing-dependencies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs a plug-in that sends multiple requests to an external web service. The plug-in must not time out if the web service has problems or responds slowly.  
  
You need to create the plug-in.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Send requests to use multiple threads.
Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
Register the plug-in step once for each web service request.
Set the HTTP connection timeout value explicitly to limit how long each connection can remain open.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse plug-ins that make external web requests should explicitly set an appropriate HTTP timeout for each call. This prevents the default HTTP-client timeout from consuming most of the plug-in execution window when the external service is slow or unavailable, allowing the plug-in to fail promptly and predictably. [Set Timeout when making external calls in a plug-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/set-timeout-for-external-calls-from-plug-ins)

**Learn more:** [Set Timeout when making external calls in a plug-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/set-timeout-for-external-calls-from-plug-ins) · [Access external web services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/access-web-services)

questions.question:
A company develops a custom connector for its cloud-based ERP system.  
  
The company needs an authentication method that the custom connector can consume.  
  
You need to configure the authentication method.  
  
Which authentication method should you use?
questions.explanation: Basic authentication is a supported authentication type for a custom connector, allowing the connector to send a username and password to the API. Windows Active Directory authentication, certificate-based authentication, and passwordless authentication are not selectable authentication types for Power Platform custom connectors.

questions.question:
A company develops a custom connector for its cloud-based ERP system.  
  
The company needs an authentication method that the custom connector can consume.  
  
You need to configure the authentication method.  
  
Which authentication method should you use?

options.text: Enable auditing for all entities that must be replicated to Azure SQL Database.
Create an export profile that specifies all the entities that must be replicated.
Enable change tracking for all entities that must be replicated to Azure SQL Database.
Create an Azure SQL Database service in the same tenant as the Dynamics 365 Sales environment.

questions.explanation:
Data Export Service replicates only entities that have change tracking enabled, and an Export Profile specifies the entities to synchronize with the destination Azure SQL Database. A destination Azure SQL Database is required; it may be in the same tenant, although current Microsoft guidance also permits a different tenant. Auditing and server-based integration are not required for this replication configuration.

**Learn more:** [Replicate data to Azure SQL Database using Data Export Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/replicate-data-microsoft-azure-sql-database)

questions.question:
You need to determine the execution mode used by the ISV solution reported by User5.  
  
Which execution mode is being used?
questions.explanation:
For a Microsoft Dataverse webhook registered to run synchronously, a failure is reported directly to the application user as an **Endpoint unavailable** error. An asynchronously registered webhook records failure details in its System Job instead.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use webhooks to create external handlers for server events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-webhooks)

questions.question:
A customer plans to design a complex business process flow that includes six custom entities and four stages for each entity. One stage will contain 15 steps.  
  
You need to explain the flaw in this design to the customer.  
  
What is the flaw in this design?

options.text: The maximum number of custom entities has been exceeded.
The maximum number of steps for a stage has been exceeded.
The maximum number of stages for an entity has been exceeded.
The minimum number of stages for an entity has not been met.
The minimum number of steps for a stage has not been met.

questions.explanation:
A business process flow can span a maximum of five unique entities/tables. Using six custom entities exceeds this limit; four stages per entity and 15 steps in a stage are within the allowed limits.\
\
**Learn more:** [Work with business process flows using code](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/developer/business-process-flows-code)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an integration that uses an Azure function to create records in the Common Data Service when leads are submitted through your company website.  
  
You create a user and assign the user the Basic User security role.  
  
You do not have administrator access to the environment being used or access to Azure Active Directory. Company policy requires service accounts for integrations, and integrations must not receive privileges beyond those necessary.  
  
You need to recommend actions an administrator should take to configure access for the Azure Function.  
  
Which three actions should you perform? Each correct selection presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create an application registration in Azure Active Directory.
Assign the system administrator security role to the application user.
Assign the Power Platform administrator role to the application user in Azure Active Directory.
Create a new security role with the minimum required permissions and assign to the application user.
Grant the application delegated permissions to the Dynamics CRM API in Azure Active Directory.
Deploy Azure B2B guest permissions to the application user.

questions.explanation:
A service-to-service Common Data Service (Dataverse) integration uses an Azure AD application registration and an application user. The application must be authorized for the Dynamics CRM API, and the application user should receive a custom security role containing only the permissions required to create the relevant records. Broad administrator roles would violate least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Register an app with Microsoft Entra ID (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/walkthrough-register-app-azure-active-directory) · [Tutorial: Create an ASP.NET Core Blazor WebAssembly app using Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/walkthrough-blazor-webassembly-single-tenant)

questions.question:
You are building a Power Apps app to manage records in the Account table in Microsoft Dataverse.  
  
You must configure a Web API request that retrieves changes from the table.  
  
You need to set the preference header for the API request.  
  
What should be included in the request header?
questions.explanation:
Dataverse Web API change tracking is initiated by including `Prefer: odata.track-changes` in the request. This asks the service to return a delta link that can subsequently be used to retrieve changes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use change tracking to synchronize data with external systems (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/nb-no/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-change-tracking-synchronize-data-external-systems)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must replace the bicycle inspection forms.  
  
Which two solutions should you use? Each answer choice presents part of the solution.  
  
**Note:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a flow that maps inspection data to Dynamics 365 Field Service
a logic app that guides the technician through the inspection
a canvas app that guides the technician through the inspection
a model-driven app based on customer service entities

questions.explanation:
A canvas app can provide the customized technician-facing inspection interface and workflow. A Power Automate flow can be triggered from that app to automate and map submitted inspection data into Dynamics 365 Field Service, which is built on Microsoft Dataverse.

**Learn more:** [Create a canvas app that can trigger a Power Automate flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/how-to/trigger-flow) · [Overview of creating apps in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/)

questions.question:
A company is building a one-way integration from Microsoft Dataverse to an external system. Data will be delivered from a webhook to an Azure Function.  
  
You need to configure the Azure Function to process the webhook data.  
  
Which class and data type must the Azure Function handle?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Dataverse webhook requests contain a body that is the JSON value of a `RemoteExecutionContext` instance. The Azure Function must therefore parse a `RemoteExecutionContext` payload in JSON format.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Webhooks to Create External Handlers for Server Events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-webhooks)

questions.question:
A company is building a Power Apps portal to collaborate with vendors.  
  
You need to add custom functionality to the portal by using JavaScript code.  
  
Which two portal entities can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Entity lists provide a custom JavaScript area in their configuration. Basic forms and multistep-form steps also contain a Custom JavaScript field for extending form functionality or presentation; this maps to Webforms.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add custom JavaScript to a form | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/configure/add-custom-javascript) · [Add custom JavaScript to a list | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/configure/add-custom-javascript-list)

questions.question:
A company is building a Power Apps portal to collaborate with vendors.  
  
You need to add custom functionality to the portal by using JavaScript code.  
  
Which two portal entities can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Grant users the Run Flows privilege.
In the app designer, ensure that the business process flow is added to the app.
Grant users the Organization Read permission on the Process table.
Open the business process flow and associate the flow with the user security roles by using the Edit security button on the command bar.

questions.explanation:
Business process flow definitions must be made available to the appropriate security roles. The System Administrator and System Customizer roles have access to new business process flows by default, while other users require the flow to be associated with their roles. The Edit security control configures those business process flow permissions.

**Learn more:** [Create a business process flow in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/create-business-process-flow)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization uses Dynamics 365 Sales and has accounting and customer service departments.  
  
You must prevent customer service users from changing the value in the balance field on Contact records. Only the accounting team must be able to edit this field.  
  
You need to create the appropriate solution without customizations.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable field security for the balance field and grant the customer service team read and update permissions.
Create a customer service form and role and a business rule that enables the balance field.
Enable field security for the balance field and grant the customer service team read permissions.
Enable field security for the balance field and grant the accounting team read permissions.

questions.explanation:
Dynamics 365 field-level security controls Read, Create, and Update permissions for an individual field through field security profiles. Enabling field security for the balance field and giving the customer service team Read permission without Update permission lets those users view the value but prevents them from changing it. The accounting team can be granted Update permission in its own field security profile.

**Learn more:** [Field level security | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/admin/field-level-security?view=op-9-1)

questions.question:
You are creating a new page for a Power Apps portal.  
  
You need to show Microsoft Dataverse data on the page.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Liquid is the template language used in Power Apps portals/Power Pages to retrieve and render dynamic Dataverse data. Dataverse-specific Liquid tags support loading and displaying that data in page content or web templates.\
\
**Learn more:** [Dataverse Liquid tags | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/configure/liquid/dataverse-liquid-tags)

questions.question:
You are a Power Apps maker who is building a chatbot for a website.  
  
The chatbot must recognize geographic attributes to support additional functionality.  
  
You need to recommend a feature.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Slot filling uses entities to recognize and extract values from user input. Copilot Studio includes built-in entities such as Country and City, so slot filling enables recognition of geographic attributes for use in the conversation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Implement slot-filling best practices - Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/guidance/slot-filling-best-practices)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an integration between Microsoft Dataverse and an external system.  
  
Messages from Dataverse must be sent to Microsoft Azure Service Bus. An Azure Function will process these messages. Events must be published directly to the Azure Service Bus ServiceEndpoint.  
  
You need to create code for the messages.  
  
Which class should you use?
questions.explanation:
`RemoteExecutionContext` is the context type Dataverse posts to Azure Service Bus remote service endpoints. It carries the execution-context data for the receiving listener, such as an Azure Function, and implements the related execution-context interfaces.

**Learn more:** [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration) · [RemoteExecutionContext Class (Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.remoteexecutioncontext?view=dataverse-sdk-latest)

questions.question:
You must resolve CustomerB's problems with the check-in application.  
  
Which two options could you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
LookUp returns only the first matching record, so it can omit other customers with the same or a partially matching last name. Filter returns all records that meet a specified condition, and Search returns all records containing the search text in the designated column or columns; either function can return the complete set of matching customers.\
\
**Learn more:** [Filter, Search, and LookUp functions - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-filter-lookup)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring a custom connector for a web service. The service is hosted in two distinct regions. Its URL contains a shared domain name and a unique subdomain for each region.  
  
The custom connector must allow the region to be specified for additional regions when the connection is created.  
  
You need to create a policy template.  
  
Which template type should you use?
questions.explanation:
The **Set Host URL** template replaces the connector host with a URL generated from a template and supports connection-parameter expressions. A region entered when creating the connection can therefore populate the unique regional subdomain while retaining the common domain. The Route Request template changes a relative path on the same service, not the host.

**Learn more:** [Set Host URL | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/policy-templates/dynamichosturl/dynamichosturl)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an asynchronous automation that calls an external API.  
  
The automation must retrieve a stored API key to connect to the API. Business users must be able to rotate the API key regularly without requiring dedicated tooling. No connector is available for the external API.  
  
You need to implement the automation.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The API key must be retrievable at run time by the automation, yet be rotatable by business users without any dedicated developer tooling. Environment variables meet this: a Secret-type environment variable references a value stored in Azure Key Vault, and business users can update it directly in the maker/admin portal (or rotate it in Key Vault) with no Plugin Registration Tool required. Secure/unsecure configuration is bound to a plug-in step and can only be changed by re-registering the step with the Plugin Registration Tool (dedicated tooling), and connection references are unusable here because no connector exists for the external API.

**Learn more:** [Use environment variables for Azure Key Vault secrets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/environmentvariables-azure-key-vault-secrets)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A model-driven app form runs JavaScript during the OnLoad event. The event retrieves an account record and changes the visibility of a form column based on one column in that record. This code portion retrieves the account record:  
  
`Xrm.WebApi.retrieveRecord('account', accountId)_`  
  
Users report that the form loads slowly.  
  
You need to improve the performance of the code that retrieves the account and changes visibility.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the code to change visibility to the success callback.
Enable the Async OnLoad app setting.
Set the options parameter to return only the column required.
Store the returned data in a global variable.

questions.explanation:
Use the `options` parameter with an OData `$select` query to retrieve only the account column needed for the visibility decision. Without `$select`, `Xrm.WebApi.retrieveRecord` returns all properties, whereas selecting specific properties reduces the response payload and is a documented performance best practice.

**Learn more:** [retrieveRecord (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-webapi/retrieverecord)

questions.question:
You must implement the Suitability Assessment Tool.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A component library provides a centralized, managed repository of reusable Power Apps components that can be shared and updated across applications, satisfying the requirement for modular components that other applications can use.\
\
**Learn more:** [Component library - Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/component-library)

questions.question:
You need to fix the issue with the eligibility assessment tool.  
  
Which two commands should you run? Each correct answer forms part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A PCF control update requires a new manifest patch version for the platform to recognize the changed control. `pac pcf version --strategy manifest` increments that version, and `pac pcf push` imports the PCF project into the current Dataverse environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Power Platform CLI pcf command group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/pcf)

questions.question:
You need to build the eligibility assessment app.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
Reusable modular Power Apps code components are created with the Power Apps component framework. The `pac pcf init` command initializes a new PCF project, which is the required starting point for developing those components.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Power Platform CLI pcf command group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/pcf)

questions.question:
You need to determine which Azure service to use for the Planning Hub application.  
  
Which service should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault securely stores and controls access to application secrets, including passwords and API keys. It meets the requirement to store sensitive credentials securely, such as the authentication secret used for the Claim Submission Portal API.\
\
**Learn more:** [Apps, API Keys, and Azure Key Vault secrets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/apps-api-keys-secrets)

questions.question:
You need to fix the funding-application issue.  
  
Which component should be used?
questions.explanation:
Environment variables hold configuration values that vary by environment and can be referenced by solution components such as Power Automate flows. They allow the test environment to use its own endpoint or other parameter value without changing the deployed flow logic.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use environment variables in Power Platform solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/environmentvariables)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a Power Platform app.  
  
The app must implement a two-way listener to an on-premises system by using Microsoft Azure Service Bus. You create an Azure Service Bus namespace and messaging entity. You must add the shared access policies.  
  
You need to choose the permissions for the messaging entity.  
  
Which two permissions should you select? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus shared access authorization rules use the Listen, Send, and Manage rights. Listen grants the ability to receive messages and perform related message handling; Send grants the ability to send messages. A two-way listener therefore requires both Listen and Send. Manage is intended for administering the namespace topology and is not required for message exchange.

**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus authentication and authorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-authentication-and-authorization) · [Azure Service Bus access control with Shared Access Signatures](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-sas)

An asynchronous post-operation Create step is invoked after the Dataverse record is committed. An Azure-aware plug-in can post its execution context to an Azure Service Bus endpoint through the Dataverse asynchronous service. A queue contract provides persistent message storage and does not require the consumer to be actively listening; failed asynchronous Service Bus posts are retried. Therefore, newly created records can remain available for Azure Function processing through temporary component outages, avoiding data loss.

**Learn more:** [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration) · [Write a custom Azure-aware plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/write-custom-azure-aware-plugin)

Solution: Register a webhook in the Dataverse instance that connects to the Azure Function. Register a webhook step that runs synchronously on the record's **Create** message in the post-operation stage.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A synchronous Dataverse webhook depends on the Azure Function endpoint being available during the create transaction. Endpoint failures cause the operation to fail and do not provide durable, queued delivery for a prolonged outage. Dataverse webhooks make only a limited retry for certain network errors; Azure Service Bus provides the queueing needed to retain messages while downstream components are unavailable.

**Learn more:** [Use webhooks to create external handlers for server events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-webhooks) · [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: Register a service endpoint in the Dataverse instance that connects to an Azure Service Bus queue.  
  
Register a step on the endpoint that executes asynchronously for the record's **Create** message in the post-operation stage.  
  
Configure the Azure Function to process records when they are added to the queue.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Dataverse asynchronous service endpoint can post the Create event context to an Azure Service Bus queue. A queue is persistent and buffers messages while a receiving Azure Function is temporarily unavailable; Azure Functions can process queued Service Bus messages when available. Restricting the asynchronous post-operation step to Create events limits the integration to newly created records.

**Learn more:** [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration) · [Azure Service Bus trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-service-bus-trigger)

questions.question:
Solution: Set up the Azure Function with a timer trigger that executes every five minutes. The function will query the Dataverse instance and process records that were created during the previous five minutes.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A rolling five-minute query window does not provide durable delivery of newly created Dataverse records. An outage lasting longer than the window can cause earlier records to fall outside the query range before processing resumes, resulting in data loss. Azure Functions timer triggers do not retry a failed function invocation; they wait until the next scheduled occurrence.\
\
**Learn more:** [Timer trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-timer)

A bank uses a Common Data Service solution to manage clients.  
  
Bank representatives conduct client credit checks while the client is present. Credit checks can take up to five minutes to finish.  
  
Bank policy requires the bank representative's app to remain blocked until the credit checks are complete.  
  
You need to show a model-driven app while credit checks are running, asking the bank representative and client to wait for the credit check to finish.  
  
Which function should you use?
questions.explanation:
`Xrm.Utility.showProgressIndicator(message)` displays a progress dialog with the supplied message and blocks the model-driven app UI until `Xrm.Utility.closeProgressIndicator` closes it. This meets the requirement to prevent the representative from interacting with the app while the credit check is still running.

**Learn more:** [showProgressIndicator (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-utility/showprogressindicator)

questions.question: What permissions does a managed identity have for Microsoft Dataverse data?

options.text: permissions assigned to the corresponding application user
permissions assigned to the user triggering the Azure resource
permissions equivalent to the environment admin role
permissions equivalent to the system administrator role

questions.explanation:
A managed identity uses its corresponding Dataverse application user for authorization. Its access to environment data is defined by the security roles and permissions assigned to that application user; it does not automatically receive environment-admin or system-administrator permissions. Microsoft documents that an Azure Managed Identity application ID can be used when creating a Dataverse application user.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage application users in the Power Platform admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization deploys Dynamics 365 Sales.  
  
You need to trigger a business rule when the main form is saved.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Write a business rule to trigger on a change of ModifiedOn field.
Set the scope of the business rule to one specific form where business rule triggers.
Set the scope of the business rule to All Forms.
Set the scope of the business rule to Entity.

questions.explanation:
A business rule scoped to a specific form applies only to that model-driven app form, allowing it to be associated with the required main form. Microsoft documents that business-rule process triggers can be registered for the `save` event; a specific-form scope identifies the relevant form rather than applying the rule to every form or to the table and server.

**Learn more:** [Create or edit how business rules are initiated](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/developer/customize-dev/create-edit-how-business-rules-initiated?view=op-9-1) · [Create a business rule in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-create-business-rule)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to identify the main cause of the issue interns report when they use the app.  
  
What is the primary cause?

options.text: Interns have the System Customizer security role but need the Environment Maker security role.
Interns have the Common Data Service User security role but need the Environment Maker security role.
Interns have the Environment Maker security role but need the Common Data Service User security role.
Interns have the Environment Maker security role but need the System Customizer security role.
Interns have the Environment Maker security role but need the Delegate security role.

questions.explanation:
The Environment Maker role allows users to create resources such as apps and connections, but it does not grant privileges to access environment data. An app user needs the applicable Dataverse end-user security role—identified here as Common Data Service User—to access and use the app’s data.

**Learn more:** [Role-based security roles for Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/database-security)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is testing a Microsoft Dataverse plug-in in an environment. The plug-in runs in post-operation mode and updates the Account entity.  
  
During testing, a user notices that the plug-in unintentionally triggers a synchronous third-party ISV plug-in.  
  
You need to change the system design to prevent the unwanted triggering of the third-party plug-in.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Disable the existing third-party plug-in by using the Plug-in Registration Tool.
Use UpdateRequest with the BypassCustomPluginExecution parameter and Execute method of the Organization service.
Update the code of the third-party ISV plug-in to ignore updates caused by the new plug-in.
Update the code of the new plug-in to use InputParameters of Plugin Execution Context.

questions.explanation:
`BypassCustomPluginExecution` on an `UpdateRequest` bypasses custom synchronous plug-in logic for that specific Dataverse operation when the request is executed through the Organization service. The caller must have the `prvBypassCustomPlugins` privilege.

**Learn more:** [Bypass custom Dataverse logic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/bypass-custom-business-logic) · [UpdateRequest Class (Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk.Messages)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.messages.updaterequest?view=dataverse-sdk-latest)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company creates a Microsoft Dataverse Custom API to encapsulate business logic.  
  
The Custom API business logic must be encapsulated so that its behavior cannot be changed or canceled.  
  
You need to configure the custom API parameter so that it cannot be customized.  
  
Which parameter value should you set?
questions.explanation:
Setting **Custom Processing Step** to **None** makes the plug-in configured for the Custom API the only logic that runs. It prevents other developers from registering additional steps that could add logic, change the operation’s behavior, or cancel it.

**Learn more:** [Create and use custom APIs (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/custom-api) · [CustomAPI tables (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/custom-api-tables)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization uses Dynamics 365 Sales and has accounting and customer service departments.  
  
Customer service users must be prevented from changing the value of the **balance** field on Contact records. Only the accounting team must be able to edit this field.  
  
You need to create the appropriate solution without customizations.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable field security for the balance field and grant the customer service team read permissions.
Create a customer service form and role and make the balance field read-only.
Create a customer service form and role and a business rule that enables the balance field.
Create an accounting form and role and a business rule that enables the balance field.

questions.explanation:
Column-level security controls access to values in an individual Dataverse field, including whether users or teams can read, create, or update it. Enable field security for the balance field and give the customer service team read permission without update permission; accounting can be assigned update permission through a field security profile. Form read-only settings and business rules do not enforce field-level authorization.

**Learn more:** [Column-level security - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/field-level-security)

questions.question:
A company is moving from an on-premises Dynamics 365 installation to a Power Platform solution. You are developing plug-ins for the new solution.  
  
You need to register the plug-ins.  
  
Which isolation mode should you use?
questions.explanation:
Dataverse plug-in assemblies in Power Platform use Sandbox isolation. Microsoft documentation states that Dataverse registrations accept the default Sandbox isolation mode, while options such as disk and the Global Assembly Cache apply to on-premises Dynamics 365 deployments.\
\
**Learn more:** [Register a plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/kk-kz/power-apps/developer/data-platform/register-plug-in) · [Tutorial: Write and register a plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/tutorial-write-plug-in)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Change tracking is enabled on the Account table in Microsoft Dataverse.  
  
You plan to retrieve delta data by using C# with the Organization Service.  
  
You need to determine which message to use.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
`RetrieveEntityChangesRequest` is the Organization Service request used to retrieve change-tracking changes for a Dataverse table. It returns change data and a data token that can be supplied on later requests to retrieve only subsequent changes.

**Learn more:** [RetrieveEntityChangesRequest Class](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.messages.retrieveentitychangesrequest?view=dataverse-sdk-latest) · [Use change tracking to synchronize data with external systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-change-tracking-synchronize-data-external-systems)

questions.question:
You are implementing custom business logic in a Power Apps portal.  
  
You need to use Liquid templates to show dynamic content.  
  
In which three entities can you include Liquid code? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Liquid supports dynamic content in a webpage’s Copy field and in content snippets, and web templates are the reusable source templates that generally contain Liquid for dynamic rendering. Page templates associate pages with layouts, while portal settings are configuration values rather than Liquid-code locations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Liquid overview | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/configure/liquid/liquid-overview) · [Web templates | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/configure/web-templates)

questions.question:
Solution: Use a table with a GUID as its primary key.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Dataverse virtual tables require each external-source table to have an associated GUID primary key so that records can be uniquely identified.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with virtual tables (entities)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/virtual-entities/get-started-ve)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a calculated column on the virtual table.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Dataverse does not support calculated columns on virtual tables. Because virtual-table data is external rather than locally stored, any required calculation must be performed by the external system or data provider.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with virtual tables (entities) (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/virtual-entities/get-started-ve)

questions.question:
Solution: Use an OData v4 provider as the data source.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Dataverse includes an OData v4 data provider for connecting virtual tables to external data sources that support the OData v4 open standard. This provides the required data-provider/data-source mechanism for virtual tables.\
\
**Learn more:** [OData v4 Data Provider configuration, requirements, and best practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/virtual-entity-odata-provider-requirements) · [Get started with virtual tables (entities)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/virtual-entities/get-started-ve)

questions.question:
Solution: Assign ownership of records to individual users.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Virtual tables in Dataverse are organization-owned and do not support assigning record ownership to individual users.

questions.question:
You need to build the customer mobile app.  
  
Which type of function expression should you use?
questions.explanation:
`LookUp` returns the first record in a table that satisfies a specified condition, making it suitable for retrieving an individual customer record. `Filter` returns a table of matching records, and `Find` returns the starting position of text within another text string.\
\
**Learn more:** [Power Apps Filter, Search, and LookUp functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-filter-lookup)

A Power Platform solution contains the following Web API request:  
  
`GET http://contoso.crm.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.1/RelationshipDefinitions?$select=SchemaName`  
  
You need to describe what this line of code does.  
  
What does the code do?

options.text: Retrieve the list of relationships between tables.
Retrieve a list of tables that are related to each other.
Retrieve a list of one-to-many relationships with other tables.
Retrieve a list of tables that have more than one relationship.
Retrieve a list of many-to-many relationships with other tables.

questions.explanation:
A GET request to `RelationshipDefinitions` retrieves relationship metadata, and `$select=SchemaName` returns only the schema name for each relationship. This entity set contains both one-to-many and many-to-many relationship definitions, so the result is a list of relationships between tables rather than only one specific relationship type.

A company needs a plug-in that submits multiple requests to an external web service. The plug-in must not time out if the web service has problems or responds slowly.  
  
You need to create the plug-in.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign the IOrganizationService object to a member variable.
Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
Register the plug-in step once for each web service request.
Set the HTTP connection timeout value explicitly to limit how long each connection can remain open.

questions.explanation:
An explicit HTTP timeout bounds how long each outbound request can wait for a response. This lets slow or unavailable external services fail quickly, preventing their default wait period from exhausting the plug-in execution time. Microsoft’s Dataverse guidance specifically recommends setting the timeout for external calls in plug-ins.

**Learn more:** [Set Timeout when making external calls in a plug-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/set-timeout-for-external-calls-from-plug-ins)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create and deploy a Power Platform solution that contains synchronous plug-ins.  
  
Users report that the solution has performance issues.  
  
You need to determine whether a plug-in is causing the performance issues.  
  
Which two tools can you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
To determine whether a plug-in is causing performance problems you use Tracing (the Plug-in Trace Log / ITracingService, which records execution detail per step) and Microsoft Dataverse analytics, whose Plug-ins dashboard in the Power Platform admin center reports metrics such as average execution time, failures, and the most active plug-ins. Solution checker only performs static analysis of code/customization quality, ISV Studio is for ISVs to monitor solution adoption and installs, and data policies (DLP) govern connector usage - none of these measure plug-in run-time performance.

**Learn more:** [Analyze plug-in performance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/analyze-performance) · [Dataverse analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/analytics-common-data-service)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You deploy a Power Platform plug-in to a production environment. The plug-in code includes detailed tracing information. You belong to the Environment Maker security role for that environment.  
  
Users report unexpected outcomes when they use the plug-in with confidential data. You verify that the plug-in operates without errors in a development environment.  
  
You need to investigate the root cause of the plug-in errors.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Send a PUT request to enable plug-in tracing for the production environment.
Send a GET request to retrieve the plugintracelogs records.
Install Plug-in profiler in the production environment by using the Plug-in Registration tool.
Reproduce and capture the errors, then debug from Visual Studio.

questions.explanation:
The plug-in already contains detailed ITracingService tracing and fails only in production against confidential data, so the goal is to read what the plug-in recorded there. Microsoft's guidance is to query the PluginTraceLog table using the Web API – a GET against /api/data/v9.x/plugintracelogs – which returns the traced message blocks without needing to reproduce the run or expose the confidential data. The Plug-in profiler (C) captures/replays the production execution context (including that confidential data) and is heavier than needed given tracing is already present, while reproducing and debugging in Visual Studio (D) won't help because the plug-in runs cleanly in the development environment. Enabling tracing via a PUT (A) is unnecessary since tracing is already emitting data.

**Learn more:** [Debug plug-ins – Use Tracing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/debug-plug-in) · [PluginTraceLog table reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/plugintracelog)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A manufacturing company uses a Common Data Service (CDS) environment to manage its parts inventory across two warehouses, modeled as business units named WH1 and WH2.  
  
Data from the two warehouses is processed separately for every part whose inventory quantities are updated. The company must automate this process by pushing inventory updates from orders submitted to the warehouses.  
  
You need to build the automation by using Power Automate flows against the CDS database. You must accomplish this with the least administrative effort.  
  
Which flow or flows should you recommend?

options.text: Two automated flows with scope Business Unit, with triggers on Create/Update/Delete on orders.
Two automated flows with scope Business Unit, with triggers on Create/Update/Delete and each flow filtering updates from each business unit.
Two scheduled flows, each querying and updating the parts included in orders from each business unit.
One scheduled flow, querying the parts included in orders in both business units.
One automated flow, querying the orders in both business units.
Two scheduled flows, each querying the orders from each business unit.

questions.explanation:
An automated Dataverse flow can run when order data changes and query the submitted orders for both warehouses. Using organization-level coverage allows a single flow to process rows across the environment, including both business units; business-unit-scoped flows would require separate coverage. Scheduled flows poll for changes rather than responding when orders are submitted and add unnecessary administration.

**Learn more:** [Create a cloud flow with Microsoft Dataverse (legacy)](https://learn.microsoft.com/is-is/power-automate/connection-cds) · [Overview of how to integrate flows with Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/dataverse/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A travel company intends to track the addresses of places its clients visit in an entity named Destination. Client details are captured in contact records. Client records include links to the places that clients visit.  
  
The company must be able to associate multiple rating records with the new address record.  
  
You discover that a custom Rating entity is incomplete.  
  
You need to extend the Rating entity so that contact, address, and rating information are contained in one location.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a 1:N relationship between the Contact system entity and the Address system entity named Destination.
Create a mapping for the Contact ג€
Create a 1:N relationship between the Address system entity and the Rating entity.
Create a 1:N relationship between the Contact system entity and the Rating entity.
Create a mapping for the Destination ג€
Create a 1:N relationship between the Destination entity and the Rating entity.

questions.explanation:
A 1:N relationship creates a lookup on the many-side table, allowing each Rating record to reference one Contact and one Destination while allowing each Contact and Destination to have many related Rating records. Therefore, Contact-to-Destination supports clients’ destination links, and Contact-to-Rating plus Destination-to-Rating stores the client, destination, and rating association. Field mappings are not needed merely to create these relationships.

You are building a model-driven app that uses data from two custom tables. The tables have a parent-child relationship, and the parent record form includes a subgrid that displays the child records.  
  
When a new child record is created from the parent form, data must automatically populate the child record form to reduce data-entry errors.  
  
You need to implement the solution.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use a Power Automate flow to read data from the parent record and update the child record upon creation.
Map table columns from the parent record to the child record.
Create a business rule that sets the default values on the child record fields to values from the parent record.
Include a quick view form on the child record showing the data from the parent record.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse column mapping on a one-to-many or many-to-one table relationship sets default values for a new related child record when it is created in the context of its parent, such as by using the child-record subgrid on the parent form. This copies the mapped parent values into the child form before the record is saved.

**Learn more:** [Map table columns in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/map-entity-fields)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must configure the app to satisfy the address-verification requirements.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer provides part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Make the address fields read-only after they have been verified.
Open a confirmation dialog when the command bar button is selected.
Enable the command bar button only when the address shows as not verified.
Clear the field indicating the address is valid when an address field changes.

questions.explanation:
Editing any address component invalidates the prior verification result, so the field that marks the address as valid must be cleared whenever an address field changes. The command-bar button should be enabled only when the address is not verified, allowing verification only when it is needed. Power Apps command enable rules can control when a command is enabled based on field values.

**Learn more:** [Define ribbon enable rules for model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/define-ribbon-enable-rules)

questions.question:
You are creating custom pages for a model-driven app.  
  
The app must show a timer control within a menu that includes a mixture of buttons and icons. Any changes made to these elements must automatically cascade to every custom page.  
  
You need to implement a solution.  
  
What should you implement?
questions.explanation:
A canvas component packages multiple controls, including a timer, buttons, and icons, as a reusable low-code UI building block. Changes to the component definition are reflected in its instances, enabling a consistent shared element across custom pages.\
\
**Learn more:** [Canvas component overview - Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/create-component) · [Add canvas components to a custom page for your model-driven app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/page-canvas-components)

questions.question:
You are building a Power Automate flow.  
  
You create an Azure Service Bus listener application that receives requests from a third-party application.  
  
When the flow calls the message queue, it must delete the message immediately when it is read.  
  
You need to make sure the queue is cleared correctly.  
  
Which method or class should be used?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus `ReceiveMode` can be set to `ReceiveAndDelete`, which treats a message as settled and removes it from the queue as soon as it is delivered to the receiver. `PeekLock` would retain the message until it is explicitly completed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Message transfers, locks, and settlement — Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/message-transfers-locks-settlement)

questions.question:
You must implement the stage field for a background verification check.  
  
Which field type should you use?
questions.explanation:
A status field represents a record’s lifecycle stage and supports valid status transitions associated with its state. This suits a background verification check, whose progress is tracked through stages.
