lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization is using Dynamics 365 Sales.  
  
You intend to use a JavaScript web resource file on the Accounts form. The file depends on two image web resource files and on the custom field `new_placeofbirth` in the Account entity.  
  
You need to add the dependencies for the JavaScript file.  
  
Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Open the web resource file, add the two image web resources to the dependency's lists, and then add the custom field new_placeofbirth to the dependency's list.
From Settings, select Customizations and then select Customize the System.
In the Account form, select Form Properties, select Non-Event Dependencies, and then add the custom field new_placeofbirth.
Select Account, select Forms, and then select the Account form.
From Web Resources, select the JavaScript file for the Account form and then select the JavaScript file.
In the Account form, select Form Properties and add the primary JavaScript file and the other two images web resources in Form Libraries.

questions.explanation:
Dependencies for a JavaScript web resource are configured on that web resource: other web resources are added to the web-resource dependency list, while an Account column such as `new_placeofbirth` is added to the column-dependency list. Opening the classic customization area and then the JavaScript resource under Web Resources provides access to those settings. Form-level Non-Event Dependencies serve a separate purpose: registering columns used by scripts that are not configured in an event handler.

**Learn more:** [Web resource dependencies (model-driven apps)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/web-resource-dependencies) · [Model-driven app form properties](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/form-properties-legacy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s communications department plans to add a publicly accessible survey page to the company’s public website.  
  
You must add the new survey page to the company’s public website and capture the page’s data in a Microsoft Dataverse environment.  
  
Explicit user credentials must not be required to write survey data to Dataverse.  
  
You need to implement authentication.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should you use?
questions.explanation:
A client secret supports server-to-server authentication, allowing the website’s backend to use a Dataverse application user/service principal to write survey submissions. This avoids requiring public survey respondents to authenticate with individual credentials. Microsoft Learn specifies that client secrets or certificates establish trust for non-interactive server-to-server Dataverse scenarios.

**Learn more:** [Use OAuth authentication with Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authenticate-oauth) · [Build web applications using server-to-server authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/build-web-applications-server-server-s2s-authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A model-driven app form uses `Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord` during the `OnSave` event to update a related record.  
  
Testing shows that the related record is not consistently updated when required.  
  
You need to ensure that the current record is saved and that the related record is updated consistently.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution. Choose two.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add logic before the update to ensure that the request is made only when the value has changed.
Enable the Async OnSave app setting.
Wrap the update in a promise.

questions.explanation:
`Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord` is asynchronous. Enabling Async OnSave allows the form’s save process to wait for promises returned by its OnSave handlers, and wrapping and returning the update operation as a promise ensures the related-record update is included in that wait. `preventDefault` cancels the save, and `disableAsyncTimeout` is only appropriate when an asynchronous handler legitimately needs more than the standard timeout.

**Learn more:** [Form OnSave event (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/events/form-onsave)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is testing a solution you built using access team templates.  
  
Users report that they cannot access rows.  
  
You need to make sure that the solution functions as expected.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign the rows to the team.
Add the users to the Access Team Members subgrid.
Assign a security role to the users.

questions.explanation:
For a system-managed access team created from an access team template, adding a user to the row’s Access Team Members subgrid creates or updates the row-specific access team and grants that user the access rights configured in the template. Users still require the necessary underlying privileges from their security roles, but role assignment alone does not add them to the row’s access team. [Use access and owner team templates for collaboration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/about-team-templates)

**Learn more:** [Use access and owner team templates for collaboration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/about-team-templates) · [Share rows using Access Team](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/user/access-team)

options.text: Copy each development to the shared environment each day.
Perform all customizations in the shared environment.
Export each developer's solution as managed.
Export each developer's solution as unmanaged.

questions.explanation:
Unmanaged solutions are used for development and remain editable after import, allowing each developer’s changes to be incorporated into the shared sandbox’s base solution. Managed solutions are deployment artifacts, cannot be directly edited, and cannot be exported after they have been imported as managed. [Microsoft Learn: Solution concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/solution-concepts-alm)

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: Solution concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/solution-concepts-alm) · [Microsoft Learn: Export solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/export-solutions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an app that uses Common Data Service.  
  
You must integrate Common Data Service with a new web application and enable that application to display Common Data Service data.  
  
You build a single-page web application by using the Web API.  
  
You need to authenticate the app by using OAuth.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL), specifically MSAL.js for a JavaScript single-page application, obtains Microsoft Entra ID OAuth tokens for accessing Dataverse through its Web API. CORS only permits cross-origin requests; it does not authenticate users.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate to Microsoft Dataverse with the Web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/authenticate-web-api) · [Use OAuth with CORS to connect a SPA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/oauth-cross-origin-resource-sharing-connect-single-page-application)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating an integration that uses Dataverse.  
  
Within a single request, the integration must create a new row when it does not already exist, or update the existing row by using supported mechanisms.  
  
You need to confirm which Dataverse features can meet this requirement.  
  
Which three Dataverse features can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Dataverse supports an atomic upsert operation that creates a row when no matching key is found and updates it when a matching row exists. Client-side code can invoke the Web API upsert request, cloud flows expose an **Upsert a row** Dataverse connector action, and plug-ins can execute an `UpsertRequest` through the organization service. Business rules are validation/business-logic rules, and PCF controls do not expose upsert as a supported control API operation.

**Learn more:** [Use Upsert to Create or Update a record](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-upsert-insert-update-record) · [Microsoft Dataverse connector reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/commondataserviceforapps/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a canvas app that will create rows in a Dataverse table.  
  
When a row is created, extra business logic must run on a related row. A cloud flow triggered by the canvas app must execute that business logic.  
  
You need to create the cloud flow.  
  
Which trigger should you use?

options.text: Dataverse - When an action is performed
Dataverse - When a row is added

questions.explanation:
The **Power Apps (V2)** trigger is used for a cloud flow invoked directly from a canvas app. It enables the app to start the flow and, when needed, supply values such as the created row identifier so the flow can perform business logic on the related Dataverse row. A Dataverse row-created trigger instead starts automatically for table changes regardless of whether the canvas app initiated them.

**Learn more:** [Use Dataverse-based flows in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/dataverse/flows-power-apps) · [Known issues with Power Apps V2 trigger in Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/flow-creation/known-issues-power-apps-v2-trigger)

You create a Power Automate flow that retrieves data from a proprietary database.  
  
You must ensure that the flow works for other users.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Share the custom connector with users.
Share the environment by giving permissions to the users.

questions.explanation:
Power Automate custom connectors are not available to other users by default, so the custom connector must be shared. The cloud flow must also be shared so that those users can use or co-own it. Microsoft documents both custom-connector sharing and cloud-flow sharing as separate access operations.

**Learn more:** [Share a custom connector in your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/share) · [Share a cloud flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/create-team-flows)

questions.question:
You are developing a model-driven app with JavaScript.  
  
You need to configure the app to show a dialog box when a form opens or when a grid on the form is sorted.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Subgrid OnLoad event occurs whenever a subgrid refreshes, including when a user sorts it by selecting a column header. A handler can be registered for that event, commonly from the form OnLoad event, to display the dialog for both required situations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Subgrid OnLoad event (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/events/subgrid-onload) · [gridContext.addOnLoad (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/grids/gridcontrol/addonload)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates two development instances, two test instances, two staging instances, and one production instance.  
  
The test team reports connection problems with the test and staging instances.  
  
You need to determine which instances the testing team can currently access.  
  
Which two URLs can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The Discovery Service returns the set of Dataverse instances that the authenticated user can access. The global discovery endpoint enumerates accessible instances across the cloud, and the regional discovery endpoint enumerates those accessible in its geography. The instance Web API endpoint is for data operations in a specified organization, not for discovering a user’s accessible instances.

**Learn more:** [Discover user organizations (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/discovery-service)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a Microsoft Power Automate cloud flow that queries Microsoft Dataverse data by using the **List rows** action.  
  
You need to configure the cloud flow to process 10,000 records during a single run.  
  
What should you do? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Set the row count parameter to 10,000.
Return the first 5,000 records and use the @odata.nextLink in the response to return the remaining records.
Create the query by using FetchXML and set the top parameter to 10,000.
Turn on pagination and set the threshold to 10,000.

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Dataverse **List rows** action has a default page limit of 5,000 rows. Enabling pagination and setting its threshold to 10,000 allows the action to automatically retrieve and return up to 10,000 records in the flow run. The configurable pagination threshold supports values up to 100,000.

**Learn more:** [Use lists of rows in flows - Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/he-il/power-automate/dataverse/list-rows)

You are setting up a Microsoft Power Virtual Agents chatbot to use the **authenticate** option for Microsoft Teams only.  
  
You need to choose the variables that return information about the signed-in user.  
  
Which two variables should you select?  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
With the Authenticate with Microsoft option for Teams, the available user-information variables are `User.DisplayName` and `User.Id`, corresponding to the display name and unique ID of the signed-in user. `User.AccessToken` and `User.IsLoggedIn` are unavailable with this option and are associated with manual authentication.

**Learn more:** [Configure user authentication - Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) · [Add user authentication to topics - Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/advanced-end-user-authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Dataverse entity and a model-driven app. The model-driven app is integrated with an external system.  
  
You plan to run business logic whenever the model-driven app creates a record. Running the business logic must not negatively affect model-driven app users.  
  
You need to implement the business logic.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Synchronous plug-in registered in the PreOperation stage
Asynchronous plug-in registered in the PostOperation stage

questions.explanation:
An asynchronous PostOperation plug-in runs after the record creation operation completes and is processed outside the synchronous transaction. This prevents external-system logic from making model-driven app users wait, unlike synchronous plug-ins or synchronous workflows.

**Learn more:** [Event Framework in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/event-framework) · [Analyze plug-in performance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/analyze-performance)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are implementing business logic for a model-driven app form by using multiple JavaScript web resources.  
  
The business logic, the number of JavaScript files, and the columns required by that business logic are expected to change frequently. Some form fields will not be visible. Non-developers will occasionally make changes to the form.  
  
You need to prevent columns referenced by the JavaScript from accidentally being removed from the form based.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Hide columns that should not be displayed.
Set all columns as business required.
Add all columns as non-event dependencies to the form.
Add columns in each JavaScript file as a dependency.

questions.explanation:
Non-event dependencies on a model-driven app form provide a central list of columns required by scripts that are not associated with a particular event handler. Registering the required columns there prevents form editors from accidentally removing them, including columns that are not displayed. Microsoft Learn states that non-event dependencies are intended for registering dependent columns and that users cannot remove those dependent columns.

**Learn more:** [Model-driven app form properties in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/form-properties-legacy) · [Web resource dependencies (model-driven apps)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/web-resource-dependencies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization deploys Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management.  
  
You must create a Microsoft Flow that runs each day.  
  
Which two possible methods can achieve this goal? Each correct answer is a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create the flow and set the flow frequency to daily and the interval to 1.
Create the flow and set the flow frequency to daily and the interval to 24.
Create the flow and set the flow frequency to hourly and the interval to 1.
Create the flow and set the flow frequency to hourly and the interval to 24.

questions.explanation:
A recurrence interval specifies the number of units defined by its frequency between runs. Therefore, an interval of 1 with a daily frequency runs every day, and an interval of 24 with an hourly frequency runs every 24 hours. Microsoft documents the recurrence frequency as the time unit and the interval as the number of those units between trigger executions.

**Learn more:** [Triggers - Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/triggers-introduction) · [Schema reference for trigger and action types - Azure Logic Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/logic-apps-workflow-actions-triggers)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a model-driven app for a company.  
  
The app must map child records to a parent record. You need to use the column mapping feature to configure the app.  
  
Which two actions can you perform? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Map the value of a Choices column on the child table to the value of a Choices column on the parent table.
Map the value of a column on the parent table that uses column values from the child table.
Map the value of columns on both the child table quick-create and main forms to the value for the same columns on the parent table.
Map the value of a single line of text column on the child table to the value of a currency column on the parent record.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse column mappings require compatible column types and formats. A Choices column can be mapped to another Choices column when the integer value for each corresponding option is identical. Mappings apply to values shown when a related row is created, and a mapping is not performed until the mapped column is included on a form. A text column cannot be mapped to a currency column, and a column whose value is derived from child records is not a valid mapping target/source for this purpose.

**Learn more:** [Map table columns in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/map-entity-fields)

questions.question:
You develop and deploy a Power Apps solution.  
  
The solution must be changed as follows:  
  
- Delete a data column.  
- Modify several views.  
- Add several charts to dashboards.  
  
You need to redeploy the app.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
A solution upgrade removes components that existed in the previous managed solution version but are not included in the newer version, so it supports deleting the data column while deploying the modified views and added dashboard charts. Solution updates and patches do not delete components.\
\
**Learn more:** [Upgrade or update a solution](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/power-apps/maker/data-platform/update-solutions) · [Application lifecycle management (ALM) basics with Microsoft Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/basics-alm)

You need to update the Power Automate flow to resolve CustomerC’s issue.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a configure run that is set to is successful.
Add a data operation that specifies the false conditions.
Add a condition containing approval hierarchy.
Add a timeout setting to the approval flow.

questions.explanation:
In this PL-400 case study, CustomerC's request is never actioned because the parts-department approver (the manager) is on sabbatical, so the approval sits unanswered indefinitely. Adding a timeout setting to the approval action lets the flow stop waiting after a defined period and escalate or reassign the approval to another person, resolving the stalled request. The other options (a run-after 'is successful' configuration, a data operation for false conditions, or an approval-hierarchy condition) do not address an approver who simply never responds.

**Learn more:** [Manage approvals in Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/sequential-modern-approvals)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization uses Dynamics 365 Sales and has accounting and customer service departments.  
  
You must prevent customer service users from changing the value of the balance field on Contact records. Only the accounting team must be able to edit this field.  
  
You need to create the appropriate solution without customizations.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable field security for the balance field and grant the customer service team read and update permissions.
Create a customer service form and role and make the balance field read-only.
Enable field security for the balance field and grant the accounting team read and update permissions.
Create an accounting form and role and make the balance field read-only.

questions.explanation:
Dynamics 365 field-level security controls read, create, and update access for a secured field through a field security profile assigned to users or teams. Enabling field security for the balance field and granting the accounting team read and update permissions ensures that accounting can edit it while customer service is not granted update access. Form settings are not a secure field-authorization mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Column-level security - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/field-level-security) · [Enable or disable field security in Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/admin/enable-disable-security-field?view=op-9-1)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company updates an existing column-bound Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) code component.  
  
You test the changes to the code component in the development environment. You then import the component into the production environment as part of a managed solution. You find that the component changes are not reflected in the production environment.  
  
You need to ensure that the changes take effect in the production environment.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Import the PCF code component to the production environment directly from Visual Studio Code by using the pac pcf push instruction.
Publish the form that uses the PCF code component in the production environment.
Increment the PCF control version property in the manifest.xml file, and then reimport the solution from development to the production environment.
Publish the PCF code component in the production environment.

questions.explanation:
A PCF code component must have its manifest control version incremented—at least the patch version—when it is updated, so Dataverse detects the new component and model-driven apps invalidate their cached version. Reimporting the updated managed solution after increasing the version makes the changed component effective.

**Learn more:** [Code components application lifecycle management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/code-components-alm) · [Common issues and workarounds (Power Apps Component Framework)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/issues-and-workarounds)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a form in a model-driven app that uses data from the Lead table in a Microsoft Dataverse instance. You add a business rule to the Lead table. The business rule shows an error when the email address is null. You set the business rule scope to **All Forms**.  
  
You configure a Power Apps portal by using the same Microsoft Dataverse instance. You create a web page by using the Lead form.  
  
You need to make sure that the same logic is applied on the Power Apps portal page.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish the goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Deactivate the business rule. Change the scope for the rule to Table and then reactivate the rule.
Replace the business rule logic with a Microsoft Power Automate cloud flow by using the Dataverse When a row is added, modified or deleted trigger.
Extend the webFormClientValidate JavaScript function to replace the business rule logic. Edit the code in Power Apps Studio. Add the function in a <script> block.
Create a JavaScript web resource and replace the business rule with a JavaScript function. Add an OnSave event handler to the Lead form.

questions.explanation:
A table-scoped business rule runs at the Dataverse server level, whereas an All Forms rule is limited to model-driven app forms; changing the rule to Table scope therefore enforces the email validation for portal submissions. Portal form JavaScript can also extend its client-validation function to validate the email value and prevent submission while displaying the error. A post-event cloud flow cannot block an invalid save, and a model-driven form OnSave web resource does not execute on a portal form.

**Learn more:** [Create a business rule in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-create-business-rule) · [Add custom JavaScript to a form](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/portals/configure/add-custom-javascript)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a plug-in for an app that enables government employees to obtain a proof-of-vaccination card.  
  
Before a proof-of-vaccination card is created, you must add the following information to a vaccination record:  
  
- Vaccination type  
- Date of vaccination  
- Name of the person administering the vaccine  
  
You need to register the plug-in.  
  
At which stage should you register the plug-in?
questions.explanation:
The PreOperation stage executes before the Dataverse core operation and within its database transaction. It is the appropriate stage for changing or adding values on the target vaccination record so those values are saved as part of creating the record. [Microsoft Learn: Event Framework in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/event-framework)

**Learn more:** [Event Framework in Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/event-framework)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a model-driven app that includes a form with several columns. Two user groups, named Group1 and Group2, will access the form.  
  
One column contains sensitive data that Group2 must not be able to read. Group1 must be able to access the column.  
  
You need to prevent Group2 users from viewing the sensitive data.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a security role for users in Group1 to grant users access to the column.
Create multiple forms. Assign a form containing the sensitive data to Group1. Assign a form that does not contain the sensitive data to Group2.
Use JavaScript to set visibility of the column based on the group of the current user.
Create a field-level security profile for Group1 users to grant the users access to the column.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse column-level security protects sensitive column values independently of the form UI. A field-level security profile can grant Group1 Read access to the secured column, while users outside that profile, including Group2, cannot view its data. Forms and JavaScript only affect display and do not enforce data access security.

**Learn more:** [Column-level security - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/field-level-security) · [Column-level security with code - Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/column-level-security)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a model-driven app that uses Microsoft Dataverse.  
  
The company needs a web application that retrieves information from the model-driven app. Requirements for the web application include:  
  
- It must be a single-page web application that uses the Web API.  
- It must display the correct company information.  
- It must authenticate by using OAuth without additional verification.  
  
You need to configure the web application.  
  
Which two methods should you use?  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Microsoft Azure Active Directory Authentication Libraries (ADAL)

questions.explanation:
ADAL and MSAL are Microsoft identity client libraries that obtain OAuth access tokens for protected web APIs. For a Dataverse single-page application, Microsoft documents MSAL.js as the supported way to authenticate users; ADAL is a legacy library whose existing applications can still function, although Microsoft recommends migrating to MSAL. NTLM and Kerberos do not provide the required OAuth flow, and multifactor authentication is an additional verification step rather than an authentication library.

**Learn more:** [Use OAuth with CORS to connect a SPA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/oauth-cross-origin-resource-sharing-connect-single-page-application) · [Migrate applications to the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/msal-migration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Microsoft Dataverse rollup fields to calculate customers' insurance exposure and risk profiles.  
  
Users report that rollup-field values are not updated when new insurance policies are written.  
  
You need to recalculate the rollup-field values immediately after a policy is created.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create new calculated fields on the customer entity for insurance exposure and risk. Create a formula to calculate the sum of values from policy records.
Change the frequency of the Calculate Rollup Field recurring job from every hour to every five minutes.
Create a plug-in that uses the update method for the rollup fields. Configure a step on the Create event for the policy entity for this plug-in.
Create a plug-in that uses the CalculateRollupFieldRequest method for the rollup field. Configure a step on the Create event for the policy entity for this plug-in.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse supports the `CalculateRollupFieldRequest` message for on-demand calculation of a rollup column. A plug-in triggered by creation of a policy can invoke that request for the related customer record and the relevant rollup field, producing an immediate recalculation rather than waiting for the scheduled rollup job.

**Learn more:** [CalculateRollupFieldRequest Class (Microsoft.Crm.Sdk.Messages)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.crm.sdk.messages.calculaterollupfieldrequest?view=dataverse-sdk-latest) · [Calculated and rollup attributes (Dynamics 365 Developer Guide)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/developer/calculated-rollup-attributes?view=op-9-1)

questions.question:
You must move an API key between environments by using a solution. You must use an environment variable whose data type is **Secret**.  
  
You need to create the environment variable.  
  
What must you create beforehand?
questions.explanation:
Secret environment variables reference secrets stored in Azure Key Vault. The Key Vault must be created and configured so Power Platform can access the secret before the environment-variable reference can be created.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use environment variables for Azure Key Vault secrets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/environmentvariables-azure-key-vault-secrets)

questions.question:
You need to add the script that handles events for the registration form.  
  
Which code segment should you use?
questions.explanation:
`formContext.data.addOnLoad(myFunction)` registers `myFunction` to run when the form data is loaded. The `addOnLoad` API is the form-data event-handler registration method for this purpose.\
\
**Learn more:** [data.addOnLoad (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/formcontext-data/addonload) · [Form data OnLoad event (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/events/form-data-onload)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to build a canvas app to manage large record sets. Users will filter and sort the data.  
  
You must implement delegation in the canvas app to reduce potential performance issues.  
  
You need to recommend data sources for the app.  
  
Which two data sources should you recommend? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
SQL Server and Common Data Service (now Microsoft Dataverse) support Power Apps delegation, allowing supported filter and sort operations to run at the data source rather than being limited to a locally retrieved subset of records. Azure Data Factory is a data-integration service, and Azure Table Storage is not a delegable canvas-app data source for these operations.

**Learn more:** [Query limitations: Delegation and query limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/delegation-overview) · [Connect to Microsoft Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/connections/connection-common-data-service)

questions.question:
Solution: Throw a custom exception that includes the message.  
  
Does the solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
For validation that cancels a synchronous Dataverse operation, the plug-in must throw an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` containing guidance for the user. This exception allows the application to show a controlled, friendly error message; an unspecified custom exception does not guarantee that behavior.\
\
**Learn more:** [Handle exceptions in plug-ins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/handle-exceptions) · [Use InvalidPluginExecutionException in plug-ins and workflow activities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/use-invalidpluginexecutionexception-plugin-workflow-activities)

questions.question:
Solution: Throw an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` that includes the message.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
For a synchronous Dataverse plug-in, throwing an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` cancels the operation and displays the supplied message to the user in the model-driven app. The message can explain the validation failure and how to correct it.\
\
**Learn more:** [Handle exceptions in plug-ins — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/handle-exceptions) · [Use InvalidPluginExecutionException in plug-ins and workflow activities — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/use-invalidpluginexecutionexception-plugin-workflow-activities)

questions.question:
Solution: Include the message in the plug-in’s output parameters.  
  
Does this solution fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
For synchronous Dataverse plug-in validation, the plug-in should throw an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` containing guidance for the user. This cancels the operation and displays that message to the user; output parameters alone do not provide the required form error message.\
\
**Learn more:** [Handle exceptions in a plug-in — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/it-it/power-apps/developer/data-platform/handle-exceptions) · [Event Framework in Microsoft Dataverse — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/event-framework)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the tracing service to record the message.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The tracing service is for diagnostic logging, not for displaying a validation error on a form. A synchronous Dataverse plug-in must throw an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` containing guidance for the user; Dataverse displays that exception message in an error dialog.\
\
**Learn more:** [Handle exceptions in a plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/handle-exceptions) · [Use ITracingService in Plug-ins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/best-practices/business-logic/use-itracingservice-plugins)

questions.question:
You are creating a custom connector in Power Apps to connect to a third-party application.  
  
The connector definition must be configured so that it is not shown to the end user.  
  
You need to choose the appropriate visibility parameter. Which parameter should you use?
questions.explanation:
The `internal` visibility setting prevents connector operations and parameters from appearing in the user interface. `none` displays them normally, `advanced` places them under an additional menu, and `important` displays them first.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a custom connector with an OpenAPI extension](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/openapi-extensions)

options.text: Add the Power Automate flow to a solution in Environment1.
Send a copy of the Power Automate flow from the default environment.
Add the Power Automate flow to a solution in the default environment.
Export the solution from the default environment and import the solution into Environment1.
Share the Power Automate flow from the default environment.

questions.explanation:
Power Automate flows are scoped to their environment. A flow that is only in the default solution view must be added to a solution in its source environment before it can be transported. Exporting that solution and importing it into Environment1 creates the solution-aware flow in the chatbot’s environment, where it can be used.

**Learn more:** [Export a solution - Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/power-automate/export-flow-solution) · [Import a solution - Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/power-automate/import-flow-solution)

questions.question:
You are developing a plug-in that connects to a third-party REST API.  
  
The API credentials must be protected so that only system administrators can view them. They also must not interfere with other system functionality.  
  
You need to store the credentials.  
  
Which method should you use?
questions.explanation:
Plug-in secure configuration stores sensitive, step-specific configuration data separately from unsecure configuration. Only system administrators have privileges to read that secure configuration, making it appropriate for third-party API credentials without affecting unrelated system functionality.\
\
**Learn more:** [Write a plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/write-plug-in)

questions.question:
Solution: Register an asynchronous plug-in that sends an HTTP request to the REST API. If the request fails, raise an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` configured for retry.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Dataverse supports retrying an asynchronous plug-in when it fails while calling an external resource. Throwing `InvalidPluginExecutionException` with `OperationStatus.Retry` causes the asynchronous service to retry the plug-in, which can handle a REST API HTTP 500 failure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Handle exceptions in plug-ins — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/handle-exceptions)

questions.question:
Solution: Register a service endpoint for an Azure Service Bus queue. Use an Azure Function to process queue messages and forward them to the REST API. Redirect failed messages to the dead-letter queue.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Azure Service Bus queues automatically redeliver a message to a receiving client when the client does not complete it, which gives an Azure Function processing the queue a built-in retry mechanism for transient failures such as an HTTP 500 from the downstream REST API. Only after the configured maximum delivery count is exhausted does Service Bus move the message to the dead-letter queue, so failures are retried before being permanently routed aside, satisfying the requirement to retry on a 500 response.

questions.question:
Solution: Register a synchronous plug-in that sends an HTTP request to the REST API. Throw an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` if the request fails.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A synchronous Dataverse plug-in that throws `InvalidPluginExecutionException` cancels and rolls back the current operation. Automatic plug-in retries are available for asynchronous plug-in steps when an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` is thrown with `OperationStatus.Retry`; a standard exception from a synchronous step does not provide that retry behavior.\
\
**Learn more:** [Handle exceptions in plug-ins (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/handle-exceptions)

questions.question:
Solution: Register a synchronous plug-in that sends an HTTP request to the REST API. Throw an `InvalidPluginExecutionException` if the request fails.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?

options.text: Initiate the iOrganizationService by passing the ID of a user with permissions to create rows in the custom table.
Ensure all users have been granted the Environment Maker role.
Set Run in the User’s Context to Calling User in the plug-in step.
Ensure all users have the Acton Behalf of Another User permission assigned to one of their security roles.

questions.explanation:
A plug-in can create an `IOrganizationService` for a specified system user ID, so its data operation runs under that user's privileges. Using an account that has only the required permission to create rows in the custom table lets all users invoke the plug-in without granting that permission, or broader roles and impersonation rights, to every user.

**Learn more:** [Impersonate a user (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/impersonate-a-user) · [IOrganizationServiceFactory.CreateOrganizationService Method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.iorganizationservicefactory.createorganizationservice?view=dataverse-sdk-latest)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop a model-driven app that uses client-side scripts extensively.  
  
Users report that forms load quickly but then become unresponsive.  
  
You need to investigate the form issues before you optimize the forms.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Remove unused forms from the app.

questions.explanation:
Client-side JavaScript runs through form event handlers and can interfere with normal form behavior or degrade performance. Disabling the handlers isolates custom scripts as the potential cause; if the problem no longer occurs, the scripts can be enabled individually to identify the faulty handler.

**Learn more:** [Isolate issues in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-apps/create-and-use-apps/isolate-model-app-issues) · [Configure model-driven app form event handlers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/configure-event-handlers-legacy)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a model-driven app to record laboratory-test details.  
  
You are asked to create a custom component that simplifies capturing multiple values from lab test results on mobile devices.  
  
You need to create the interface for the dataset if the mobile devices lose their network connection. Which method should you use?
questions.explanation:
For a Power Apps Component Framework dataset control, `updateView` receives dataset values and is called when property-bag values change, including both datasets and offline status. Dataset values cannot be initialized in `init`, so the dataset interface belongs in `updateView`.

**Learn more:** [StandardControl (Power Apps component framework API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/reference/control) · [StandardControl.updateView (Power Apps component framework API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/component-framework/reference/control/updateview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a canvas app to retrieve user sign-in information from Microsoft Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) when a person searches for details about an end user.  
  
You create an Azure Function that retrieves the required information by using JSON.  
  
You need to ensure that the application operates correctly.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a Power Automate flow to import data.
Create a custom connector by using the Azure Function API.
Use app designer in the Power Platform admin center.
Create an API definition for the Azure Function.

questions.explanation:
A canvas app can invoke an Azure Function’s REST operations through a custom connector. The function’s API must be described with an API definition, such as an OpenAPI definition, so the connector has the operation and data-contract metadata it needs; the custom connector can then be used by the canvas app.

**Learn more:** [Custom connectors for canvas apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/register-custom-api) · [Create a custom connector from an OpenAPI definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/connectors/custom-connectors/define-openapi-definition)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying a Power Apps app that uses a custom connector for ServiceNow.  
  
The app loads very slowly for some users. You determine that every user retrieves all records from ServiceNow.  
  
The app must load only the incidents assigned to each user.  
  
You need to restrict the number of records returned by the connector.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Apply a Lifecycle Services asset scope

questions.explanation:
Custom connector policy templates can change connector request behavior at runtime. A query-string policy template can add or override the ServiceNow request parameter that filters incidents by the current user’s assignment, so the service returns only the relevant records instead of the full set.

**Learn more:** [Policy overview for custom connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/policy-templates) · [Set Query String Parameter policy template](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/policy-templates/setqueryparameter/setqueryparameter)

questions.question:

The code must be able to read the record's Id column.  
  
You need to configure the manifest.  
  
Which solution should you use?
questions.explanation:
A manifest `property` defines a configurable Dataverse data value that a PCF component expects and makes it available at runtime. A read-only input property can supply the record’s Id column to the component. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a model-driven app for Contoso, Ltd. You add a button to the account page. The button must send a text message to the company's account team when a user selects it.

During the month-end financial-close process, a company runs a batch job that copies all orders to a staging database.  
  
The staging database calculates outstanding amounts owed by clients and must process all historical data.  
  
You need to ensure that the integration process includes only data affected during the month.  
  
Which two approaches can achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Use change tracking on the orders and run the integration to retrieve new orders and the orders that have the total amount changed in the last month.
Create a system view with the orders that have the Modified On field in the last month and run the integration on this subset.
Use change tracking on the order lines and run the integration every week and retrieve only the order lines that have been created or deleted in the last month.
Create a system view with the order lines that have the Modified On field in the last month and run the integration on this subset.

questions.explanation:
Outstanding amounts are determined from order-line detail, so incremental processing must identify affected order lines. Dataverse change tracking supports synchronization by returning records that changed since the prior extraction, including deleted records. Alternatively, a system view filtered by the order line `Modified On` date limits the integration to line records modified during the month. Tracking or filtering only order headers does not reliably provide the required line-level history.

**Learn more:** [Use change tracking to synchronize data with external systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-change-tracking-synchronize-data-external-systems)

questions.question:
You need to decrease the number of Azure Consumption API calls made by User2.  
  
Which markup segment should you use?
questions.explanation:
The `rate-limit-by-key` policy limits calls independently for each `counter-key`. Using the request IP address as the key and allowing only one successful call in each 60-second renewal period throttles that caller, reducing User2's API calls. `increment-condition` can ensure that only responses with status code 200 are counted.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure API Management policy reference - rate-limit-by-key](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/rate-limit-by-key-policy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the following code:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810122158-pv7fkhfq.png)  
  
You have a contact record with the GUID `991bf2fd-d40c-4752-9984-26b7c0455b69`.  
  
You need to set the contact record as an account’s primary contact when creating the account.  
  
Which two code segments can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A contact can be associated as an account’s primary contact either by using the legacy lookup object with `logicalname` and `id`, or by setting the single-valued navigation property with the `primarycontactid@odata.bind` annotation and a `/contacts(<GUID>)` entity-set path. `@odata.context` is response metadata rather than an association operation, and a URL cannot be assigned directly to the lookup property.

**Learn more:** [createRecord (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-webapi/createrecord)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that offers API access. You plan to connect to that API from a canvas app by using a custom connector.  
  
You need to obtain information from the API developers to create the custom connector.  
  
Which two file types can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Power Apps supports creating a custom connector by importing either an OpenAPI definition, which describes the REST API’s operations and data structures, or a Postman collection, which the connector wizard imports and converts to an OpenAPI definition.

**Learn more:** [Create a custom connector from an OpenAPI definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/connectors/custom-connectors/define-openapi-definition) · [Create a custom connector from a Postman collection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/define-postman-collection)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a new implementation that will use Dynamics 365 Field Service.  
  
A developer adds two custom tables to the solution in a development environment. The custom tables contain lookup columns to Field Service tables.  
  
The developer creates a new test environment and imports the solution. The developer receives an error stating that dependencies are missing.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for the missing-dependencies issue.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Add the Field Service tables to the solution.
Add the custom tables to the solution.
Install the Field Service application in test.

questions.explanation:
Lookup columns create dependencies on their referenced tables. Because the referenced Field Service tables are provided by the Dynamics 365 Field Service application, that application must be installed in the test environment before importing the custom solution. Microsoft documents that Field Service is installed per Power Platform environment.

**Learn more:** [Install Dynamics 365 Field Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/field-service/install-field-service)

questions.question: A company has implemented Dynamics 365 Sales. An email notification needs to be sent automatically to the sales manager whenever a business process completes. You need to ensure the email is sent. What should you create on the process completed trigger?
questions.explanation: On the process completed trigger of a Business Process Flow, you configure a workflow, since workflows in Dynamics 365 support the 'Send Email' step and can be triggered automatically when the process reaches completion. Action steps are used to run custom actions/business logic, and data steps are used for retrieving or manipulating data, neither of which natively sends email notifications the way a workflow does.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a canvas app for a bank. Consumers will enter information in the app when applying for a loan.  
  
The app's input form must show fields prompting the consumer for their first name, last name, address, and requested loan amount.  
  
Immediately after a consumer enters a value in the LoanAmount field, the column background color must change. It must become red when the consumer enters more than $5,000 and green for values less than or equal to $5,000.  
  
You need to implement the required behavior.  
  
Which option should you use?

options.text: Add a business rule to the form.
Add a formula to the LoanAmount field.

questions.explanation:
Canvas apps use Power Fx formulas to calculate control properties automatically as input values change. A formula on the LoanAmount control or its containing data card's Fill property can return red when the entered amount is greater than 5,000 and green otherwise, providing immediate conditional background formatting.

**Learn more:** [Add and configure controls in canvas apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/add-configure-controls) · [Understand behavior formulas for canvas apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/working-with-formulas-in-depth)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deploys managed customizations by using two solutions: SolutionA and SolutionB. The solutions share components with each other.  
  
A SolutionA developer needs a new development environment. Customizations made in SolutionA must not interfere with customizations made in SolutionB.  
  
You need to import solutions to prepare the environment.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Import SolutionA as managed and SolutionB as unmanaged.
Import SolutionA and SolutionB as unmanaged.
Import SolutionA as unmanaged and SolutionB as managed.
Import SolutionA and SolutionB as managed.

questions.explanation:
Unmanaged solutions are used for active development, whereas managed solutions are deployed packages whose components cannot be edited directly. Importing SolutionA as unmanaged permits its developer to make changes, and importing SolutionB as managed protects SolutionB’s customizations from direct changes in that environment.

**Learn more:** [Solution concepts with Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/alm/solution-concepts-alm) · [Solution layers in Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/solution-layers)

questions.question:
You are building a FetchXML query.  
  
The query must return data from a table and return filtered data from a related table.  
  
You need to configure the FetchXML query.  
  
Which two elements should you use? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The `attribute` element specifies a column from an entity or linked entity to return in a FetchXML query. The `link-entity` element joins a related table and can be used with filters to apply criteria to values in that related table.\
\
**Learn more:** [FetchXml reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/fetchxml/reference/) · [link-entity element](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/fetchxml/reference/link-entity)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s communications department plans to add a publicly available survey page to the company’s public website.  
  
You must add the new survey page to the company’s public website and capture data from the page in a Common Data Service environment.  
  
Explicit user credentials must not be needed to write survey data to Common Data Service.  
  
You need to implement authentication.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should you implement?
questions.explanation:
OAuth 2.0 supports server-to-server authentication to Dataverse by using an application identity and access token, so the website can write survey submissions without requiring each public respondent to provide credentials. An X.509 certificate may be used as a confidential-client credential within an OAuth flow, but OAuth 2.0 is the authentication mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate with Microsoft Dataverse web services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authentication) · [Build web applications using server-to-server authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/build-web-applications-server-server-s2s-authentication)

You are developing a Power Platform solution. The solution connects to a third-party accounting system by using a Web API through a Power Apps app that automatically exchanges contacts with sales data.  
  
You have the following code (line numbers are included for reference only):  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783847767480-yxmg5nhg.png)  
  
You need to ensure that the code synchronizes only data that has not been synchronized previously.  
  
Which code segment should you insert at line 02?
questions.explanation:
`Prefer: odata.track-changes` enables Dataverse Web API change tracking. It returns a delta link that can be used for later requests to retrieve only data changed since the initial extraction or last synchronization.

**Learn more:** [Use change tracking to synchronize data with external systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-change-tracking-synchronize-data-external-systems) · [Compose HTTP requests and handle errors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/compose-http-requests-handle-errors)

questions.question:
Solution: Add the custom connector to a managed solution, export that managed solution, and then import it into the production environment.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Custom connectors can be packaged in solutions and migrated to a target environment by exporting and importing the solution. A managed solution is suitable for deploying the connector to production, while the single-tenant Microsoft Entra ID application restricts authentication and access to users in its tenant.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create custom connectors in solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/finance/get-started/custom%20connectors/custom-connectors-solutions)

questions.question:
Solution: Export the custom connector by using Postman. Then import the connector into the production environment by using Postman.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Postman collection is used to create or define a custom connector, not to migrate an existing connector between Power Platform environments. Importing a Postman collection requires connector settings such as authentication to be configured again. Custom connectors should be migrated by exporting the solution and importing it into the target environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a custom connector from a Postman collection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/define-postman-collection) · [Create custom connectors in solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/finance/get-started/custom%20connectors/custom-connectors-solutions)

questions.question:
Solution: Publish the custom connector to AppSource.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
AppSource publishing is intended to distribute a connector broadly, whereas the requirement is to keep the connector visible and accessible only within the tenant. Custom connectors can be shared within an organization; Microsoft certification is used when sharing outside the organization is needed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Share a custom connector in your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/share)

questions.question:
Solution: Export the custom connector by using the maker portal. Then import the connector into the production environment by using the maker portal.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A custom connector can be moved to a target environment by exporting its definition and importing it there. Its Microsoft Entra ID authentication remains governed by the Azure Function's single-tenant app registration, so only identities from that tenant can authenticate to the protected service. Custom connectors in Power Apps and Power Automate are shared only with intended users, and sharing is performed within the organization.\
\
**Learn more:** [Share a custom connector in your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/share) · [Create custom connectors in solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/finance/get-started/custom%20connectors/custom-connectors-solutions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a Power Apps app to manage records in the Account table in Microsoft Dataverse.  
  
You must configure a Web API request to retrieve changes from the table.  
  
You need to set the preference header for the API request.  
  
What should you include in the request header?
questions.explanation:
When synchronizing changes from a Dataverse table via the Web API, the client sends Prefer: odata.track-changes on the request. The @odata.nextLink annotation is used purely to page through the results of a single query and is unrelated to change tracking; @odata.context only identifies the response's EDM type and offers no synchronization capability. The @odata.deltaLink annotation returned once the full change-tracked result set has been retrieved is what the client persists and reuses to pull only the records that have changed since the prior call, which is the mechanism that fulfills a "retrieve changes" requirement.

**Learn more:** [Page results using OData from Microsoft Dataverse Web API - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query/page-results)

A company intends to implement an integration between Microsoft Dataverse and Azure Service Bus.  
  
When an Account row is updated and the Credit Limit is set to more than $25,000, row information must be posted to an Azure Service Bus queue. The prior Credit Limit value must also be included.  
  
You use the Microsoft Power Platform CLI to create the plug-in package.  
  
You need to implement an interface.  
  
Which interface should you implement next?
questions.explanation:
An Azure-aware Dataverse plug-in uses the notification service that implements `IServiceEndpointNotificationService` to post the current execution context to a configured Azure Service Bus endpoint. A plug-in step can use a pre-image to make the prior Credit Limit available in that context. `IServiceEndpointPlugin` and `IWebHttpServiceEndpointPlugin` instead define listener contracts for one-way and REST Service Bus relay endpoints, not the service used by the Dataverse plug-in to post to a queue.

**Learn more:** [Write a custom Azure-aware plug-in (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/write-custom-azure-aware-plugin) · [Azure integration (Microsoft Dataverse)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/azure-integration)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a custom application in Azure to process resumes for the HR department. The app will monitor for resume submissions and parse the resumes. You need to parse the resumes and save the contact and skills information into the Common Data Service.  
  
Which mechanism should you use?
questions.explanation:
Power Automate provides triggers that can monitor for new resume submissions (for example, a new file being uploaded or an email arriving), can call parsing services (such as AI Builder or Cognitive Services) to extract contact and skills information, and can use the native Dataverse (Common Data Service) connector to create or update records with that parsed data—all without writing extensive custom code. In contrast, a Dataverse plug-in only executes in response to Dataverse (CDS) message events and cannot monitor external resume submission sources; a raw Web API call would require you to build your own polling/monitoring and orchestration logic; and a custom workflow activity extends classic Dataverse background workflows triggered by Dataverse events, not external file submissions. This makes Power Automate the appropriate low-code integration mechanism for this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Exam PL-400 topic 1 question 14 discussion - ExamTopics](https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/microsoft/view/87463-exam-pl-400-topic-1-question-14-discussion/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company manages capital equipment for an electric utility company and has a SQL Server database containing maintenance records for the equipment.  
  
Technicians who service the equipment use the Dynamics 365 Field Service mobile app on tablet devices to view scheduled assignments. They use a canvas app to display and update the maintenance history for each piece of equipment.  
  
Managers use a Power BI dashboard that displays Dynamics 365 Field Service and real-time maintenance data.  
  
Because demand is increasing, managers must be able to work in the field as technicians.  
  
You need to design a solution that enables managers to work from a single screen.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the maintenance history app to the Field Service Mobile app.
Add the manager Power BI dashboard to the Field Service mobile app.
Create a new maintenance canvas app from within the Power BI management dashboard.
Add the maintenance history app to the Power BI dashboard.

questions.explanation:
The Power Apps visual can embed an existing canvas app in Power BI, allowing managers to use the maintenance-history app from their existing Power BI dashboard. The visual can pass context-aware data from Power BI to the canvas app, combining the dashboard’s Field Service and real-time maintenance insights with the ability to view and update maintenance history in one interface.

**Learn more:** [Power Apps visual for Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/powerapps-custom-visual)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a canvas app that realtors use to identify neighbors of properties that are for sale.  
  
The **OnStart** property contains the following code:  
  
```  
ClearCollect(collectNeighborList, Filter(NeighborList, Status = `Active"));  
ClearCollect(collectRealtorList,CompanyList);  
ClearCollect(collectRegions, RegionList)  
```  
  
The app is performing more slowly than expected.  
  
You need to resolve the issue.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Replace all instances of the ClearCollect method with the connect method.

Replace the existing code segment with the following code segment Concurrent (ClearCollect(collectNeighborList, Filter(NeighborList, Status = ג€Activeג€)), ClearCollect(collectRealtorList,CompanyList),ClearCollect(collectRegions, RegionList))

Replace the existing code segment with the following code segment: ClearCollect(collectNeighborList, Filter(NeighborList, Status = ג€Activeג€)); Concurrent(ClearCollect(collectRealtorList,CompanyList)); Concurrent(ClearCollect(collectRegions, RegionList))

questions.explanation:
Power Fx evaluates formulas chained with semicolons sequentially. `Concurrent` evaluates multiple independent formulas at the same time and is specifically recommended in an app’s `OnStart` property to reduce data-loading time. The three `ClearCollect` operations have no dependency on one another, so putting them together in a single `Concurrent` call reduces the startup wait to approximately the longest individual data request.

**Learn more:** [Concurrent function - Power Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/reference/function-concurrent)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to set up the trigger for the **Priority** field in the **Account** entity.  
  
Which expression should be used?
questions.explanation:
The requirement is a trigger field that fires 10 days after an Account record is created. The correct approach is a calculated column (for example Priority_Trigger) whose formula computes the trigger date by adding 10 days to the creation date: ADDDAYS(10, CreatedOn). A downstream process can then act when the current date reaches that value. DIFFINDAYS(CreatedOn, now()) only returns the elapsed number of days rather than a target date to trigger on, and the other options use the wrong units, argument order, or non-existent functions. ADDDAYS is a valid Dataverse calculated-column date function.

**Learn more:** [Define calculated columns](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/define-calculated-fields) · [Dataverse formula/function reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/power-fx/formula-reference-formula-columns)

Which version identifier should you use?
questions.explanation:

You add the forms to a solution and export the solution as managed. When you import the managed solution into the test environment, an error indicates that the solution is missing a component.

What causes the import error?

options.text: The web resources were not added to the form before adding the form to the solution.
The solution must be exported as an unmanaged solution.
The web resources were not added to the solution before exporting.
A copy of the form must be made before adding to the solution.

questions.explanation:
JavaScript used by form event handlers is stored as a web resource, which is a solution-aware component that must be included in the solution package. Exporting forms without their referenced web resources leaves a required component unavailable in the target environment, producing a missing-dependency import error. Microsoft documents that missing dependencies occur when a solution references components absent from the target environment and that the missing components must be included in the source solution before export.

**Learn more:** [Missing Dependencies During Solution Import in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/power-platform/dataverse/working-with-solutions/missing-dependency-on-solution-import) · [Create or edit model-driven app web resources in Power Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/create-edit-web-resources)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must ensure that users are able to create the required charts.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a quick view form to show the Accounts entity.
Configure filter fields in the Annual revenue field.
Add the Facility field to the account form.
Delete the Annual revenue field from the account form.
Create a view with annual revenue sorted lowest value to highest value.

questions.explanation:
Interactive dashboard charts use configured filter fields for filtering and drill-down behavior. Annual revenue must therefore be configured as a filter field. The Facility field must be included on the Account form so account records can contain the facility classification needed to chart research facilities and hospitals. Views provide the data source for charts, but sorting annual revenue does not enable the required interactive filtering or classification.

questions.explanation:

A client requires the system to send an email when a button on their customer contact form is selected.  
  
You need to invoke the action from JavaScript. Which two functions accomplish this? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
`Xrm.WebApi.online.execute` invokes a single Dataverse action, function, or CRUD request. `Xrm.WebApi.online.executeMultiple` invokes a collection of such requests, which can contain an action request. Either method can therefore invoke the email-sending action; record creation and record update methods do not themselves execute it.

**Learn more:** [Xrm.WebApi.online.execute (Client API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-webapi/online/execute) · [Xrm.WebApi.online.executeMultiple (Client API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-webapi/online/executemultiple)

options.text: Add a response property to the custom API.

questions.explanation:
