questions.explanation:
A model-driven form can accept custom parameters passed through `Xrm.Navigation.openForm` when those parameters are defined in the form XML. In an exported solution's `customizations.xml`, adding `querystringparameter` elements inside a `formparameters` element specifies the custom parameters the form accepts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure a form to accept custom querystring parameters (model-driven apps)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/configure-form-accept-custom-querystring-parameters) · [openForm (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-navigation/openform)

questions.question:
Solution: Export the solution, modify the `customizations.xml` file, and add a `querystringparameter` element to the XML.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The goal in this repeated-answer set is to configure a receiving model-driven form so it will accept a custom parameter passed to it (for example via Xrm.Navigation.openForm). Microsoft's documented, supported way to make a form accept a custom query string parameter is to open the form editor, choose Form Properties, and add the parameter on the Parameters tab (or edit the FormXml). That is exactly what this solution does, so it achieves the goal. The competing solution in this set (adding a web resource that sets formContext.data attributes) does not, because JavaScript alone cannot register the form to accept an unexpected parameter. Note that custom parameter names must contain an underscore and cannot begin with 'crm_'.

**Learn more:** [Configure a form to accept custom querystring parameters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/configure-form-accept-custom-querystring-parameters)

questions.question:
Solution: In the form editor, add an event handler for the data parameter.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A model-driven form accepts a custom value passed through `Xrm.Navigation.openForm` only when that value is configured as an allowed custom query-string parameter in the form’s Parameters settings (or in FormXml). An event handler can process an accepted parameter during form load, but it does not configure the form to accept the parameter.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure a form to accept custom querystring parameters (model-driven apps)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/configure-form-accept-custom-querystring-parameters) · [openForm (Client API reference) in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-navigation/openform)

questions.question:
Solution: In the form editor, add a web resource that sets `formContext.data.attributes`.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A model-driven form accepts custom parameters only when their names and data types are defined in the form properties’ Parameters tab or in the form XML. A web resource that sets `formContext.data.attributes` does not register an allowed custom parameter, so it cannot configure the form to receive the contact-type value passed through `Xrm.Navigation.openForm`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure a form to accept custom querystring parameters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/configure-form-accept-custom-querystring-parameters) · [openForm (Client API reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/reference/xrm-navigation/openform)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Dynamics 365 developer working on a model-driven app.  
  
You add a button to an entity form and to that entity’s view that invokes a JavaScript function. Selecting the button causes an error.  
  
You determine that the JavaScript function calls another JavaScript function in a separate web resource.  
  
You need to fix the error.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: In the JavaScript web resource, add the missing web resource as a dependency.
Add &ribbondebug=true to the app URL and run the Command Checker tool.
From the Ribbon Workbench, add the missing JavaScript web resource as a CustomRule in EnableRules.

questions.explanation:
A JavaScript web resource can declare another web resource as a dependency. In a model-driven app, dependent web resources are loaded together with the primary JavaScript web resource, including when that primary script is registered for a ribbon command. Configuring the missing JavaScript web resource as a dependency therefore makes the called function available.

**Learn more:** [Web resource dependencies (model-driven apps)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/web-resource-dependencies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to make sure that Adventure Works Cycles can track information from visitors at bike fairs.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: a Power Automate flow that connects with the bike fair Power Apps app to create a lead in Dynamics 365 Sales
a Power Automate flow that generates a new customer record in SharePoint.
a Power Automate flow to capture customer data from the bike fair Power Apps app in SharePoint and create a lead in Microsoft Teams.
a business process flow in Dynamics 365 Sales for capturing leads.

questions.explanation:
Dynamics 365 Sales uses lead records to track prospective customers. A Power Automate flow can take visitor information submitted through the bike-fair Power Apps app and create a lead in Dynamics 365 Sales; a business process flow only guides users through stages of an existing business process.

**Learn more:** [Create or edit leads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/create-edit-lead-sales) · [Manage leads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/lead-management-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure the solution so that it meets the requirements for driving-record verifications.  
  
Which two possible methods can achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create an Azure Logic Apps connector.
Use a connector provided by the driving record verification service.
Share a custom connector for the driving record verification service with a member of the talent department.
Share the flow with a member of the talent department.

questions.explanation:
Power Automate can use a connector supplied by an external service directly. When the service does not have an appropriate prebuilt connector, its API can be exposed through a custom connector; custom connectors are not available to other Power Apps and Power Automate users by default, so the connector must be shared with the talent-department user who needs to use it. Sharing a flow alone does not create or grant access to a connector for the external verification service.

**Learn more:** [Build and certify custom connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/developer/register-custom-api) · [Share a custom connector in your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/share)

A company develops a custom connector for its cloud-based ERP system.  
  
The company needs an authentication method that the custom connector can use.  
  
You need to configure the authentication method.  
  
Which authentication method should you use?
questions.explanation:
Power Platform custom connectors support Basic authentication as an authentication type; it uses a username and password when creating the connector connection. Windows Active Directory authentication, biometric authentication, and two-factor authentication are not supported custom-connector authentication types for this configuration. [Specify connection parameters — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/connection-parameters)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Common Data Service rollup fields to calculate customer insurance exposure and risk profiles.  
  
Users state that rollup-field values are not updated when new insurance policies are created.  
  
You need to recalculate the rollup-field values immediately after a policy is created.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create new fields on the customer entity for insurance exposure and risk. Write a workflow process that is triggered when a new policy record is created to calculate the sum of values from policy records.
Update the Mass Calculate Rollup Field job to trigger when a new policy record is created.
Change the frequency of the Calculate Rollup Field recurring job from every hour to every five minutes.
Create a plug-in that uses the CalculateRollupFieldRequest method for the rollup field. Configure a step on the Create event for the policy entity for this plug-in.

questions.explanation:
Dataverse supports on-demand rollup-column calculation through `CalculateRollupFieldRequest`, which targets the record containing the rollup column and identifies the rollup field to calculate. Registering a plug-in on the policy entity’s Create event allows the associated customer’s rollup field to be recalculated immediately after the policy is created, rather than waiting for scheduled rollup jobs.

**Learn more:** [CalculateRollupFieldRequest Class](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.crm.sdk.messages.calculaterollupfieldrequest?view=dataverse-sdk-latest) · [Calculated and rollup attributes (Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement Developer Guide)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customerengagement/on-premises/developer/calculated-rollup-attributes?view=op-9-1)
